purpose: Subject galaxy and distance from Mathlib for every roadmap. Distances run from 0 (the targets can be stated and proved from Mathlib now) to 10 (several research-level theories must be built first). Generated by scripts/classification.py; do not edit by hand.

sources.classification: research/blueprint/classify: subject classes of each roadmap's principal references (zbMATH Open API) and a distance judged against the pinned Mathlib and Tau Ceti baseline.
sources.estimate: data/classification-estimates.json: provisional values for roadmaps whose classification has not finished.

AInfCohomology.rationale: The library has Witt vectors, the tilt, Fontaine's theta map and B_dR^+, but no perfectoid rings or spaces, no formal schemes, no pro-étale site of an adic space, no PD envelopes, and no crystalline, de Rham–Witt or prismatic cohomology or décalage operator Lη. The targets (Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, Česnavičius–Koshikawa) are recent research theorems that rest on all of these theories.

AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli.rationale: Tau Ceti defines abelian varieties over a field, with commutativity from Mathlib's rigidity theorem, and Cartier duality for finite locally free commutative affine group schemes. There are no abelian schemes over a base, algebraic spaces, Picard functors or dual abelian schemes, polarizations, Weil pairings, relative de Rham cohomology or Serre–Tate/Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory. That is several layers of graduate and research-level theory (Mumford, Faltings–Chai I, Artin representability).

AdditiveCombinatorics.rationale: Mathlib already has Plünnecke–Ruzsa, additive energy, Freiman homomorphisms, Szemerédi regularity and Roth's theorem for 3-term progressions via the corners theorem. Nothing exists for Gowers norms, nilmanifolds and nilsequences, Szemerédi's theorem for longer progressions, transference or the Green–Tao–Ziegler inverse theorem, whose proofs are among the longest in the field. The endpoints (Green–Tao, linear equations in primes) need several research-level layers on top.

AdelicAlgebraicGroups.rationale: Mathlib provides the adele and idele rings, restricted products and Haar quotient measures, and Tau Ceti has reductive affine group schemes over a field with dynamic parabolics. Missing are adelic points of group schemes over a number field, rational parabolics and relative roots over non-closed fields, Siegel sets and Borel–Harish-Chandra reduction theory, Tamagawa measures and strong approximation: about two layers of graduate theory.

AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons.rationale: Mathlib has the étale and pro-étale topologies on schemes and derived categories of abelian categories, and Tau Ceti has Huber pairs and Spa, but there is no étale cohomology, no six-functor formalism, no diamonds or v-sheaves, no Nagata compactification and no de Jong alterations. The targets are the final sections of Scholze's Étale cohomology of diamonds, which rest on all of those theories.

AdicEtaleGeometry.rationale: Tau Ceti has Huber rings, Spa(A,A⁺) with rational subsets, the structure presheaf and a rational-cover sheaf criterion. It does not yet have adic spaces as a category, and there are no completed tensor products or fibre products, étale or pro-étale sites of adic spaces, formal schemes, pseudocoherent modules or perfectoid spaces. The nonnoetherian approximation target (a special case of Fargues–Scholze IV.4.19) is research-level analysis on top of all of this.

AdicSpacesPartII.rationale: Tau Ceti has Huber pairs, strongly noetherian Huber rings, restricted power series, Spa and its structure presheaf, but not yet adic spaces as a category. Missing are completed tensor and fibre products, analytification and GAGA, formal schemes and generic fibres, Kiehl-type coherent theory, étale sites, dagger algebras and sousperfectoid families. That is several layers of classical rigid geometry plus perfectoid-era research theory.

AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights.rationale: Mathlib and Tau Ceti have analytic modular and cusp forms, q-expansions, Hecke operators and newforms. There are no modular curves as schemes over Z[1/N] with a Hodge bundle, no Katz modular forms or q-expansion principle, no Hasse invariant or theta operator, and no local Galois theory (tame inertia characters, finite flat group schemes) for Serre's weight recipe. That is several layers of arithmetic geometry before the targets.

AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry.rationale: Mathlib has schemes and affine space, the module-theoretic Grassmannian functor, fibred categories, the stack condition for pseudofunctors, and Zariski-local representability by schemes. It has no projective bundles or Grassmannian schemes, Hilbert/Quot schemes, algebraic spaces, algebraic stacks with atlases, coarse spaces, Artin's criteria or resolution of singularities. Each is a substantial graduate or research-level layer (EGA/FGA, Knutson, Laumon–Moret-Bailly, Artin, Bierstone–Milman).

AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.rationale: Mathlib has Galois categories with fibre functors and fundamental groups, finite étale algebras over a ring, and group and continuous group cohomology. There is no étale fundamental group of a scheme with its arithmetic exact sequence, and there are no unipotent étale or de Rham fundamental groups, Tannakian categories, Coleman integration, p-adic heights or Selmer varieties. Mochizuki's reconstruction theorem and Kim/quadratic Chabauty sit near the research frontier and rest on p-adic Hodge theory and Galois duality, neither of which is built.

AnalyticNumberTheory.rationale: Mathlib has the Riemann, Hurwitz, Dirichlet and Dedekind zeta and L-functions with continuation, nonvanishing on Re(s)=1 and Dirichlet's theorem on primes in progressions. Tau Ceti adds truncated Perron formulas and a smoothed Wiener–Ikehara limit, so the prime number theorem in progressions is close. Explicit formulas, zero-density and mean-value estimates, Halász-type theorems, prehomogeneous and Selberg zeta functions and Bost–Connes systems are further graduate-to-research layers.

ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights.rationale: Mathlib has Weil heights on number fields and projective space with the Northcott property, and Tau Ceti has abelian varieties over a field and canonical heights on elliptic curves. There are no hermitian bundles or arithmetic degrees, no abelian schemes over rings of integers, no Néron or semistable models, no Faltings metric or height, and no compactified moduli of polarized abelian varieties. The comparison theorems rest on Faltings–Chai degeneration theory, which is entirely absent.

ArithmeticDynamics.rationale: Mathlib has Weil heights on projective space with the upper bound under homogeneous polynomial maps, the Northcott property, periodic points and resultants, so canonical heights for morphisms of P^N are about one layer away. Polarized morphisms of general projective varieties need the Weil height machine for ample line bundles, local dynamics needs Berkovich spaces, and equidistribution of small points needs adelic metrics and arithmetic intersection theory. Several research-level layers are missing.

ArithmeticGaloisDuality.rationale: Mathlib and Tau Ceti have group cohomology, continuous cohomology of topological representations, Tate cohomology with Herbrand quotients and an abstract class-formation layer. There is no local or global reciprocity isomorphism, no local Tate duality, no Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence, no global Euler characteristic formula or Poitou–Tate duality, and no passage to compact p-adic coefficients. That is several layers of standard graduate Galois cohomology.

ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations.rationale: Mathlib has the absolute Galois group with its Krull topology, decomposition and inertia subgroups, arithmetic Frobenius elements and topological representations, and Tau Ceti has ramification groups for function-field places and a Chebotarev development. Missing are continuous Galois representations over p-adic coefficient rings with lattices, Brauer–Nesbitt, tame and fundamental characters, Grothendieck's monodromy theorem and Weil–Deligne representations, Artin and Swan conductors with Hasse–Arf, and Tate modules of abelian varieties: about two layers of graduate theory.

ArithmeticKTheory.rationale: Mathlib has class groups and class numbers, Dirichlet's unit theorem and the Grothendieck group of a monoid, but no algebraic K-theory beyond these: no plus or Q-construction, no K₂ or Milnor K-theory, no localization sequence, no Borel stable cohomology of arithmetic groups and no étale Chern classes. The integral and 2-primary structure theorems (Soulé, Rognes–Weibel) rest on motivic cohomology and the Bloch–Kato/Milnor conjectures, none of which exists.

ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces.rationale: Mathlib has Lie groups, manifolds with corners, properly discontinuous actions and singular homology, and Tau Ceti has relative singular homology and abstract double-coset Hecke rings. There are no symmetric spaces of reductive groups or Cartan involutions, no arithmetic quotients or Borel–Serre compactification, no local systems with sheaf-cohomology comparison on orbifolds, and no Hecke correspondences on cochain complexes with Poincaré–Verdier duality. That is several research-level layers, on top of the adelic reduction theory, which is also missing.

ArithmeticQuantumTopology.rationale: Tau Ceti has braid groups, the Temperley–Lieb (Jones) representation, the Alexander polynomial and grid diagrams, and Mathlib has braided and rigid monoidal categories. There are no ribbon categories or quantum groups, no colored Jones polynomials or Reshetikhin–Turaev invariants, no surgery presentations or Kirby calculus, no Habiro completions, and no hyperbolic ideal triangulations or extended Bloch groups. Kirby's theorem and Habiro's unified invariant are deep, and the later stages reach the research frontier.

ArithmeticStatistics.rationale: Mathlib has Minkowski's lattice-point theorem, Hermite's finiteness theorem for bounded discriminant, class groups and Selmer groups of Dedekind domains, and Tau Ceti proves Mordell–Weil over number fields with explicit 2-Selmer groups. Missing are the integral invariant theory of binary quartic and ternary cubic forms, orbit parametrizations, lattice-point counts in cusped fundamental domains, uniformity estimates for sieving to infinitely many local conditions, and p-adic orbit densities: several layers of research-level geometry of numbers.

AutomorphicBundles.rationale: Mathlib has analytic modular forms and q-expansions, and Tau Ceti has reductive affine group schemes and fppf quotient torsors. There are no Shimura data, Shimura varieties or canonical models, no associated vector bundles of torsors on schemes, no toroidal or minimal compactifications and no Fourier–Jacobi expansions. The canonical and subcanonical extension theorems (Harris, Milne, Lan) rest on compactification theory that is itself far from the library.

AutomorphicCongruences.rationale: The library has analytic modular forms, level-N Eisenstein series, newforms and Hecke rings. It has no Iwasawa algebras or characteristic ideals, Selmer complexes, Hida families, unitary Shimura varieties with Klingen/Siegel Eisenstein series and Fourier–Jacobi expansions, deformation rings with patching, Kato or Beilinson–Flach Euler systems, or p-adic local Langlands. The targets (Skinner–Urban, Fouquet–Wan, Castella–Liu–Wan, Burungale–Castella–Skinner) are frontier results resting on all of these.

AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups.rationale: Mathlib has Lie groups, universal enveloping algebras, Haar measure, Schwartz functions with the Fourier transform and adeles, and Tau Ceti adds reductive group schemes over fields. There are no (g,K)-modules or Harish-Chandra modules, no Casselman–Wallach/Bernstein–Krötz globalization, no relative Lie algebra or continuous cohomology with the van Est isomorphism, no adelic automorphic forms of moderate growth, constant terms or cusp forms, and no restricted tensor-product factorization. That is several layers of graduate and research-level analysis on reductive groups.

AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations.rationale: Mathlib and Tau Ceti have analytic modular forms, newforms with Hecke operators, the absolute Galois group and topological representations. There is no étale cohomology of modular curves or Kuga–Sato varieties, no Eichler–Shimura congruence relation, no Weil conjectures, no Shimura curves or Hilbert modular varieties, no local Langlands correspondence for GL₂ and no p-adic comparison theorems. Constructing these representations with full local–global compatibility (Deligne, Carayol, Saito) needs many unbuilt research-level theories.

AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII.rationale: Everything missing for the rank-two case (étale cohomology, Shimura varieties, local Langlands) is missing here too. On top of that, the roadmap needs compact unitary and PEL Shimura varieties with Kuga–Sato local systems, Igusa varieties and the stabilized trace formula, eigenvarieties, dagger/rigid cohomology on toroidal compactifications, and nearby-cycle monodromy arguments. The targets (Shin, Chenevier–Harris, Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne, Caraiani, Varma) are at the current research frontier.

AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors.rationale: Mathlib has Schwartz functions and the Fourier transform on real vector spaces, Poisson summation on ℝ, the Mellin transform, Haar measures, adeles, and Dirichlet L-functions with functional equations. There are no Schwartz–Bruhat functions or adelic Poisson summation, no Tate zeta integrals, no smooth or admissible representations of p-adic and real GL_n, no Whittaker models, Satake isomorphism or L-groups, and no Godement–Jacquet or Rankin–Selberg theory. Several graduate and research-level layers of representation theory are missing.

AutomorphicPadicLFunctions.rationale: Mathlib has measures on ℤ_p with the Amice transform, CM fields, Dedekind zeta functions and ζ(−n) through Bernoulli numbers, and Tau Ceti has finite ray class groups, but there are no Hecke characters with infinity types, p-power ray class towers, Hilbert modular forms with a q-expansion principle, overconvergent cohomology, CM abelian varieties, Igusa towers or unitary Shimura varieties. The Barrera Salazar–Williams, Deligne–Ribet, Katz and Eischen–Harris–Li–Skinner constructions are research-level results that need all of these, the unitary ones close to the frontier.

AutomorphicSpectralTheory.rationale: Mathlib has Haar measures on quotients and Tau Ceti adds eigenbases for compact self-adjoint operators, Stone's theorem for unbounded self-adjoint operators and a fundamental domain for PSL(2,ℤ), but there are no direct integrals of Hilbert spaces, trace-class or Hilbert–Schmidt operators, Eisenstein series or intertwining operators on reductive groups, Arthur truncation or weighted orbital integrals. Langlands' spectral decomposition and Arthur's invariant trace formula are long research-level theories on top of automorphic forms on reductive groups, which are themselves missing.

BorelRegulators.rationale: Mathlib has the unit regulator of a number field, the residue of the Dedekind zeta function at s = 1, Lie algebra cochains in degrees at most two and arithmetic subgroups of SL₂(ℤ), but there is no higher algebraic K-theory or plus construction, no rational Hurewicz theorem, no continuous or relative Lie algebra cohomology with van Est, no Borel–Serre theory for SL_n over rings of integers, no Dedekind zeta values at negative integers and no Beilinson regulator. Borel's rank and regulator theorems and the comparison with Beilinson need several research-level layers on top of these.

BunGAndNewtonStrata.rationale: Mathlib has Witt vectors and the classification of one-dimensional isocrystals, and Tau Ceti has reductive group schemes over a field, cocharacter Levi subgroups, split root data and fppf quotient torsors, but there are no G-isocrystals, σ-conjugacy classes B(G), Kottwitz or Newton maps, perfectoid spaces, v-stacks, relative Fargues–Fontaine curves or Banach–Colmez spaces. Bun_G as an ℓ-cohomologically smooth Artin v-stack, with its Newton strata and charts, is recent Fargues–Scholze work that rests on all of these theories.

ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology.rationale: Mathlib has the small étale site of a scheme with a Grothendieck abelian category of sheaves, étale points and sheaf cohomology, and Tau Ceti has Huber pairs and Spa(A,A⁺), but there are no adic spaces with étale sites, formal schemes or specialization maps, strict localizations, nearby cycles over valuation rings, proper-support pushforward, or traces and Poincaré duality for rigid curves, and even the scheme-theoretic base change theorems are absent. Huber's comparison, invariance, constructibility and duality theorems are research-level results that need several of these layers first.

ClassicalArithmeticCompletion.rationale: Most of the elementary layer is already present: Mathlib has quadratic reciprocity for Jacobi symbols, Gauss and Jacobi sums, Möbius inversion, the Chinese remainder theorem, linear recurrences, Bernoulli numbers, Pell equations, sums of two and four squares, Frobenius numbers, Mahler measure and Kronecker's theorem, and Tau Ceti adds Smith normal form, resultants, discriminants and Kummer–Dedekind. What is missing is higher power-residue reciprocity through class field theory, Christol's theorem, Hermite and rational canonical forms, Pisot–Salem theory and Galois module structure (Noether's normal integral bases, locally free class groups), about one layer of standard graduate theory.

ClassicalSerreModularity.rationale: Tau Ceti has newforms with Hecke eigenvalues and a partial Chebotarev development, and Mathlib has absolute Galois groups, the cyclotomic character and continuous representations, but there are no Galois representations attached to modular forms, no Serre weights or conductors, no deformation rings, patching or modularity lifting, no potential modularity or compatible systems, and no Fontaine–Laffaille, Barsotti–Tate or p-adic local Langlands theory. Khare–Wintenberger's proof and the Dieulefait–Pacetti route through Pan's 2022 theorem are landmark research results resting on all of these.

CohomologyComparisons.rationale: Mathlib has Witt vectors, the tilt, Fontaine's θ, B_dR^+ as a ring, divided power algebras, Kähler differentials and the cyclotomic character, but none of the theories being compared exists: there is no A_inf, crystalline, log-crystalline, de Rham or prismatic cohomology, no B_cris or B_st, no Hyodo–Kato complex and no p-adic étale cohomology of rigid spaces. The roadmap sits above the A_inf, crystalline, derived de Rham and prismatic roadmaps, and its targets are recent integral p-adic Hodge theory (Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, Česnavičius–Koshikawa, Bhatt–Scholze).

ColemanIntegration.rationale: Mathlib has ℂ_p, convergent power series over any complete field, Mahler expansions on ℤ_p, Gauss sums and complex Dirichlet L-functions, and Tau Ceti has restricted power series, but there is no p-adic logarithm with a chosen branch, no Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic L-function, no wide opens or overconvergent de Rham cohomology with Frobenius lifts, and no Coleman functions or p-adic polylogarithms. Coleman's construction and the formula for L_p(θ,k) need a graduate layer of p-adic analysis and p-adic L-functions and then a research-level layer of rigid cohomology and Frobenius continuation.

ColemanPowerSeries.rationale: Mathlib has cyclotomic extensions with norms of ζ−1, the p-adic cyclotomic character, measures on ℤ_p with the Amice transform and Weierstrass preparation, and Tau Ceti has unit filtrations and Teichmüller lifts for local fields, but there are no local cyclotomic towers ℚ_p(μ_{p^n}) with norm-compatible units, no completed group rings ℤ_p[[ℤ_p^×]], no Coleman norm operator or ψ, no Coleman map and no cyclotomic units. That is one to two layers of standard graduate Iwasawa theory (Coleman, Iwasawa, Rodrigues Jacinto–Williams §§9–12).

CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompati.rationale: Mathlib has continuous group cohomology, topological representations and arithmetic subgroups of SL₂(ℤ), and Tau Ceti has abstract Hecke rings and finite-level newforms, but there are no towers of modular or Shimura curves with completed cohomology, no completed Hecke algebras with their Galois representations, no locally algebraic vectors or admissible Banach representations, no (φ,Γ)-modules or Colmez's p-adic local Langlands correspondence, and no Galois deformation rings or patched modules. Emerton's local–global compatibility theorem and the Paškūnas and Tung refinements are frontier results that combine all of these with the Galois representations of modular forms, which are also absent.

CompletedCohomologyPartII.rationale: The library has group cohomology, continuous cohomology of topological groups, Mittag-Leffler systems of sets and profinite groups, but no arithmetic locally symmetric spaces for a general reductive group, no Borel–Serre models, no Iwasawa algebras of compact p-adic analytic groups (Lazard's noetherianity), no derived inverse limits or lim¹ sequences, no admissible Banach representations and no Shimura towers. The targets (Emerton 2006, the Calegari–Emerton finiteness package, Scholze's §4.2 towers) are research-level theorems that need all of these layers first.

ComplexComparisonPartII.rationale: Schemes, Proj, quasicoherent and finitely presented sheaves of modules, sheaf cohomology on sites, Kähler differentials and singular homology are available, and Tau Ceti has a holomorphic sheaf on ℂ. There is no analytification of schemes in the baseline (the PR196 layers are proposals), no complex analytic spaces, no Oka coherence or Cartan Theorem B, no cohomology of O(n) on projective space, no hypercohomology or algebraic de Rham complex, and no algebraic spaces or Chow lemma. That is several substantial layers of classical graduate theory (Grauert–Remmert, Serre, Grothendieck) before GAGA and the de Rham comparison.

ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciproc.rationale: CM fields, the Weierstrass ℘-function of a period lattice, the j-invariant of a Weierstrass curve, Artin symbols and an abstract class-formation framework are present. Global class field theory (reciprocity and the existence theorem), the analytic uniformisation of complex elliptic curves by lattices, CM types and reflex norms, CM abelian varieties, algebraic Hecke characters and the Shimura–Taniyama reciprocity law are all absent, and CM.2 also needs the canonical-model theory of ShimuraVarieties V5. That is several layers of classical but deep theory, one of them research-level.

ComputationalNumberTheory.rationale: The certificate side is partly present: Lucas primality, Fermat probable primes, Minkowski-bound class-number-one criteria, Dirichlet's unit theorem and Sturm bounds for finite-index levels. Missing are Miller–Rabin and AKS with their proofs, polynomial factorisation over finite fields, unit-index and class-group certificates, modular symbols and Hecke matrices, and validated interval or ball numerics for L-values. That is roughly one layer of standard graduate algorithmic theory plus the modular-symbol and L-value inputs from other roadmaps.

CrystallineCohomology.rationale: Mathlib supplies the algebraic starting data: divided-power structures, DP morphisms and sub-DP ideals, the divided-power algebra as a quotient, canonical divided powers on ℤ_p, Witt vectors with Frobenius and Verschiebung, Kähler differentials and exterior algebras. There are no PD envelopes, no algebraic de Rham complex, no crystalline site, crystals or PD Poincaré lemma, no finiteness of coherent cohomology for proper schemes, no de Rham–Witt complex and no log structures. The semistable Hyodo–Kato and BLM/Langer–Zink targets sit on several further layers of research-level theory.

DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra.rationale: Mathlib already has local and Artinian rings, adic completion, Noetherian power-series rings, Krull dimension, regular sequences, the Rees Ext-characterisation of regular sequences, projective-dimension formulas for quotients by regular sequences, regular local rings and derived categories. Missing are Schlessinger's criterion and deformation functors, completed tensor products, Cohen–Macaulay and complete-intersection theory, Auslander–Buchsbaum, perfect complexes with Tor-amplitude and derived completion. On top of that one layer of graduate commutative algebra sits the research-level Taylor–Wiles–Kisin and Calegari–Geraghty patching machinery.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity.rationale: Mathlib has the small étale and pro-étale topologies on schemes, and Tau Ceti has point counts of Weierstrass curves and deg(1−Frobenius) = #E(F_q), though not yet the Hasse bound. Nothing further is present: no étale cohomology with ℓ-adic or constructible coefficients, Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula, Poincaré duality, Künneth or Leray theory, Lefschetz pencils and vanishing cycles, Rosati positivity or Weil numbers. Weil I and II are deep established theorems resting on essentially all of SGA 4, 4½, 5 and 7.

DerivedDeRhamCohomology.rationale: Mathlib has Kähler differentials, the naive cotangent complex (Algebra.Extension.Cotangent and H1Cotangent), exterior algebras, filtered objects and derived categories of abelian categories. There are no simplicial commutative or animated rings, no enhanced (∞-categorical) module categories, no full cotangent complex or derived exterior powers, no derived I-completion, no derived de Rham complex with Hodge or conjugate filtration, no quasisyntomic site and no log cotangent complex. The comparison targets (Bhatt 2012, BMS2) are research-level and also need the missing crystalline PD theory.

DiamondEtaleCohomology.rationale: Tau Ceti has Huber rings and pairs, the adic spectrum Spa as a spectral space with rational subsets and a structure presheaf. Mathlib has the tilt, Fontaine's θ, condensed sets and the pro-étale topology on schemes. There are no adic spaces as geometric objects, no perfectoid rings or spaces, no v-sheaves or diamonds, no étale cohomology of adic spaces (Huber) and no ∞-categorical enhanced derived categories with left completion or hyperdescent. The ECD targets are research-level and sit on all of these missing layers.

DiamondSixOperations.rationale: The library has 1-categorical Kan extensions, the quasicategory predicate, pretriangulated homotopy categories and Tau Ceti's affinoid adic spectra. It has no enhanced stable ∞-categories of sheaves with fibrewise Kan extension, no diamonds or v-stacks, no étale D_ét with four operations, no proper-support pushforward or exceptional inverse image, no dualizing complexes and no Verdier biduality. ECD §§22–25 are research-level theorems that come after the whole diamond étale-cohomology stack, itself still unbuilt.

DiamondsAndVStacks.rationale: The point-set and categorical groundwork is largely present: spectral spaces and maps, pro-constructible sets, Stonean spaces with Gleason's theorem, light condensed sets, descent data for pseudofunctors, and Tau Ceti's Huber pairs with spectral Spa. There are still no adic spaces glued from affinoids, no perfectoid rings or spaces, no tilting equivalence, no pro-étale or v-sites of perfectoid spaces, no w-localisation and no diamonds or small v-stacks. Several layers of research-level theory (Huber, Scholze 2012, ECD §§7–15) must be built first.

DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence.rationale: Mathlib has Liouville's theorem and transcendence of Liouville numbers, Dirichlet approximation and continued fractions, Siegel's lemma, multiplicative heights on number fields with the Northcott property, and the analytic part of the Lindemann–Weierstrass proof. Roth's theorem, successive minima, the subspace theorem, Gelfond–Schneider, Baker's linear forms in logarithms with explicit constants, E- and G-functions and effective Thue/S-unit bounds are absent. These are deep but largely self-contained graduate-to-research proofs, with Baker–Wüstholz zero estimates and the subspace theorem at research level.

DirichletPadicLFunctions.rationale: Mathlib already provides most of the inputs: p-adic measures on ℤ_p with the Amice transform, the Mahler basis, Dirichlet L-functions and their values at negative integers via Bernoulli numbers, Gauss sums, the Dedekind-zeta residue limit and the q-expansion of level-one Eisenstein series. Tau Ceti adds the Teichmüller character. Missing is one layer of standard graduate theory (Washington, Iwasawa, RJW): generalised Bernoulli numbers, pseudo-measures and the Kubota–Leopoldt interpolation, Kummer congruences, the p-adic logarithm on algebraic extensions with Leopoldt's formula, the pole and residue on weight space, and Eisenstein measures.

DrinfeldModulesAndTModules.rationale: Mathlib has skew polynomial rings (the carrier for L{τ}) and the completion F_q((1/t)) at infinity. Tau Ceti has function fields of curves with places, divisors and Riemann–Roch. There are no Drinfeld modules or Carlitz module, no C_∞, no analytic uniformisation, no Tate modules of Drinfeld modules, no moduli stacks or Satake compactifications, no Anderson t-motives or Tannakian and difference-Galois theory, and no Goss L-values. DM.0–DM.2 are one layer of graduate theory (Rosen, Goss); DM.3–DM.8 add several layers of research-level theory (Pink, Taguchi, Taelman, Papanikolas).

EffectiveDiophantineMethods.rationale: Tau Ceti proves the Mordell–Weil theorem for elliptic curves over number fields, with 2-Selmer groups, naive heights and the Néron–Tate pairing. Mathlib has Siegel's lemma but no lattice reduction. Missing are LLL and short-vector certificates, certified complex and p-adic numerics, the Baker–Matveev explicit bounds, Jacobians of higher-genus curves, Coleman integration, Chabauty–Coleman zero bounds, the Mordell–Weil sieve and quadratic Chabauty with p-adic heights. That is several layers of graduate and research-level theory, the last stage relying on recent nonabelian Chabauty work.

EllipticCurveModularity.rationale: Mathlib has Weierstrass elliptic curves with point groups and j-invariants, and Tau Ceti has Mordell–Weil over number fields, isogenies of elliptic curves, newforms with strong multiplicity one and GL₂ Hecke rings. The deduction here consumes full Serre modularity (Khare–Wintenberger), Faltings' isogeny theorem, Eichler–Shimura quotients of J₀(N), Galois representations attached to newforms with Carayol's local–global compatibility, conductors and Tate modules of elliptic curves, and modular curves with their Jacobians. None of these is present, and each is among the deepest established theorems in the subject.

EllipticKTheory.rationale: Tau Ceti has K₀ of exact, abelian and triangulated categories, classes of line bundles on schemes, and elliptic-curve point groups and isogenies. Mathlib has the Picard group of a commutative ring. There is no higher algebraic K-theory (Quillen Q-construction, Waldhausen or Thomason–Trobaugh K-theory of perfect complexes), no localisation or coniveau sequences, no Milnor K₂ or tame symbols, no Adams operations, no regular proper arithmetic surfaces, and no scheme-level Pic⁰(E) ≅ E(F). Several layers of research-level K-theory must precede the curve computations and Bloch's symbols.

EllipticRegulators.rationale: Present are the Weierstrass ℘-function and period lattices, Jacobi theta and Hurwitz-zeta analysis, the Dedekind eta function, and in Tau Ceti the Mordell–Weil regulator and unit regulators. Everything the targets rest on is absent: K₂ of curves, Deligne cohomology and the symbol regulator, the Bloch–Wigner and elliptic dilogarithms, complex uniformisation of elliptic curves, CM Hecke characters with Deuring's L-function comparison, modular units and Beilinson's modular-curve theorem, modularity for ER.7, and syntomic regulators. Bloch's CM theorem and Beilinson–Schappacher–Scholl are research-level results on top of these theories.

EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceCompari.rationale: The library has root pairings and root data, a reductive predicate for affine group schemes over a field (Tau Ceti), Haar measures and a Kummer-theory fragment of Galois cohomology. Every construction the roadmap needs is absent: stable conjugacy and Tate–Nakayama/Kottwitz invariants, transfer factors and orbital integrals, the Arthur trace formula and its stabilisation, Hitchin fibrations, affine Springer fibres and the decomposition theorem behind Ngô's fundamental lemma, Igusa varieties, local Langlands for GL_n and Harris–Taylor's towers. The endpoint (Caraiani–Scholze 2024) is at the current research frontier.

EnhancedDerivedSheaves.rationale: The 1-categorical and triangulated layer is in Mathlib: derived categories, K-injective complexes, t-structures, Dold–Kan, Grothendieck abelian categories with enough injectives, locally presentable categories, sheaf cohomology and the quasicategory predicate. The enhancement itself is absent: mapping spaces, limits and Kan extensions in quasicategories, straightening/unstraightening, stable and presentable ∞-categories with the adjoint functor theorem, dg nerves, symmetric monoidal ∞-categories, animated rings, left completion and hyperdescent. That is most of Higher Topos Theory and Higher Algebra, several layers of research-level foundations.

EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves.rationale: Mathlib provides the étale site of a scheme with abelian sheaf categories, derived categories with t-structures, sheaf cohomology on sites and the free group of algebraic cycles with pushforward. Tau Ceti adds Kummer cocycle classes for fields. The finite-coefficient étale foundations this roadmap imports (constructible sheaves, proper base change, Rf_!, trace formula) are not in the baseline, and neither are f^!, smooth purity, Poincaré–Verdier duality, rational equivalence, Chern classes and cycle maps, perverse t-structures or the BBD decomposition theorem, which also needs Weil II. That is several layers of SGA 4, 4½, 7 and BBD.

EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems.rationale: Tau Ceti supplies continuous group cohomology, Kummer theory, Frobenius prime sets and auxiliary primes from its Chebotarev development, and 2-Selmer groups of elliptic curves. Mathlib supplies exterior algebras. Missing are local Tate duality and Poitou–Tate for p-adic representations, Selmer structures with propagated local conditions, ray class fields from global class field theory, Iwasawa algebras, Fitting ideals and Gorenstein orders, and all of the Euler, Kolyvagin and Stark system theory with its descent arguments. The last is research-level (Mazur–Rubin, Burns–Sakamoto–Sano) and sits on graduate Galois-cohomological prerequisites not yet built.

EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture.rationale: Mathlib has cyclotomic extensions, norms of ζ−1 and class groups. Tau Ceti has Kummer maps, Herbrand quotients and Chebotarev auxiliary primes. Missing are Iwasawa algebras with the structure theory of Λ-modules and characteristic ideals, cyclotomic units and their index formula, semilocal units with Coleman power series, the Kubota–Leopoldt measure, global class field theory with Poitou–Tate duality, and the general Euler-system descent this roadmap imports. The Kolyvagin–Rubin and Greither proofs are research-level arguments resting on those several missing layers.

ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction.rationale: Apart from root pairings with their dual (flip) and Tau Ceti's root data, nothing the roadmap consumes exists. There are no smooth representations of p-adic groups or Bernstein centres, no Weil groups or L-parameters, no stack of L-parameters, no Bun_G on the Fargues–Fontaine curve with lisse sheaves, no Hecke stacks or geometric Satake, and no stable ∞-categorical enhancement. The targets (Fargues–Scholze's semisimple parametrisation and spectral action, and the Laumon–Rapoport–Stuhler/Hausberger realisation in equal characteristic) are current-frontier results resting on many unbuilt theories.

ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod.rationale: Mathlib has additive characters, Fourier analysis on ZMod with Gauss sums, Lagrange's four-square theorem and Dirichlet's theorem on primes in progressions. Tau Ceti has a Wiener–Ikehara Tauberian theorem and Gaussian Fourier integrals. There are no Weyl differencing or van der Corput estimates, no circle-method decomposition into major and minor arcs, no singular series or local densities, and no Vinogradov mean-value theorem. The endpoints need several further layers: Bourgain–Demeter–Guth decoupling, Vaughan/Heath-Brown prime identities with Siegel–Walfisz major arcs, Birch's forms theorem and the determinant method, all research-level.

FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems.rationale: Tau Ceti defines abelian varieties over a field with Hom and End groups, base change, products and isogenies. Mathlib has absolute heights on number fields and projective space with a Northcott instance. The proof rests on objects that are all absent: Tate modules of abelian varieties with Galois action, polarisations, Zarhin's trick, dual abelian varieties, moduli of polarised abelian varieties with level structure and their compactifications, Néron models and semistable reduction, finite flat group schemes of type (p,…,p), and Faltings heights with their isogeny estimates. Faltings' theorems are deep established results on top of several research-level theories.

FarguesFontaineDiamonds.rationale: The algebra behind the curve is partly present: Witt vectors, the tilt, untilts and Fontaine's θ in Mathlib, and Huber pairs with Spa in Tau Ceti. The 'existing' curve is the AdicSpaces roadmap's construction; the baseline has no glued adic spaces, no Y_F or X_F = Y_F/φ^ℤ, no perfectoid spaces, no diamonds or Spd ℚ_p, no ECD 15.6 site comparison, and no left-completed D_ét needed for F5. The Fargues–Scholze comparisons and annular estimates are research-level and sit on all of these missing theories.

FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums.rationale: FF.0–FF.1 are essentially in Mathlib: Galois fields and their classification, Frobenius, additive and multiplicative characters, and Gauss and Jacobi sums with their norm identities. Hamming distance and Tau Ceti's generator and parity-check matrices of linear codes give a start on FF.4. The distance comes from FF.2, which imports the Weil and Deligne bounds through ℓ-adic trace functions and Weil II, several research-level layers that are not built, plus the missing factorisation algorithms, Galois rings and Reed–Solomon/BCH theory.

FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeThe.rationale: Tau Ceti already has Cartier duality for finite locally free commutative affine group schemes, with base change, on top of Hopf-algebra and fppf foundations. Mathlib has Witt vectors with Frobenius and Verschiebung. Missing are connected–étale sequences, p-divisible groups and their Tate modules, Dieudonné theory, Raynaud's e < p−1 uniqueness theorem, Fontaine–Laffaille modules, Breuil–Kisin modules (including Kisin's and Liu's classifications and the dyadic case) and Grothendieck–Messing, which needs the crystalline site. One graduate layer and several research-level layers must be built.

FunctionFieldArithmetic.rationale: Tau Ceti already covers much of FA.0–FA.1: places of function fields, divisors and the product formula, Weil differentials and canonical divisors, Riemann–Roch, finiteness of the divisor class group, the different divisor, repartitions and strong approximation. Mathlib adds F_q((1/t)). Still missing are topological adeles with self-dual Haar measure and Poisson summation, upper ramification filtrations with Riemann–Hurwitz and Artin–Schreier–Witt theory, and local and global class field theory for function fields. Also missing are curve zeta functions with the Weil bound and Chebotarev for covers, and the reduction theory, cusp forms and Satake dictionary for reductive groups over K. That is several layers, the last one research-level (L. and V. Lafforgue).

GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer.rationale: Mathlib has the adele ring of a number field with its finite and infinite parts. Tau Ceti has classical modular forms, newforms with strong multiplicity one and GL₂ Hecke rings. None of the representation-theoretic layer exists: smooth admissible representations of GL₂ over local fields, Whittaker and Kirillov models, newvector theory and local factors, automorphic forms and cuspidal spectral decomposition for GL₂ over number fields, converse theorems, and local Langlands for GL₂. Also missing are the invariant and simple trace formulas with their transfer inputs, Jacquet–Langlands, cyclic base change and Langlands–Tunnell. These are deep established theorems resting on several unbuilt research-level theories.

GL2ModularityLifting.rationale: Tau Ceti has GL₂ Hecke rings, classical newforms with strong multiplicity one and Chebotarev auxiliary primes, and Mathlib has the local commutative algebra needed for patching. Every arithmetic input is missing: Galois representations attached to Hilbert modular forms, quaternionic Hecke modules on Shimura curves, global and local Galois deformation rings with Kisin's potentially Barsotti–Tate rings, Taylor–Wiles–Kisin patching, integral p-adic Hodge theory, p-adic local Langlands for GL₂(ℚ_p) and completed-cohomology local–global compatibility. The modern strand (Paškūnas, Hu–Tan, Tung, Pan 2022) is at the research frontier and rests on all of these.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory.rationale: Tau Ceti has exact structures on categories and ExactK0, including finitely generated projective modules, and Mathlib has nerves, the geometric realisation of simplicial sets and homotopy groups. Missing are the Q-construction with π₁ ≅ K₀, the plus construction and group completion, Quillen's additivity, resolution, dévissage and localisation theorems, Waldhausen categories and the S-construction, spectra and infinite loop spaces, nonconnective K-theory with Bass negative groups, and products. That is a graduate layer (Quillen) plus several layers of research-level homotopical foundations (Waldhausen, Thomason–Trobaugh, Schlichting).

GeneralizedHeegnerCycles.rationale: Beyond Tau Ceti's classical newforms, Hecke rings, elliptic-curve isogenies and abstract algebraic cycles in Mathlib, the library has nothing this roadmap uses. Missing are modular curves and universal elliptic curves as schemes, Kuga–Sato varieties and their projectors, CM theory and ring class fields, Chow groups with étale cycle classes and Abel–Jacobi maps, syntomic and p-adic Hodge regulators, BDP and Hsieh anticyclotomic p-adic L-functions, Kolyvagin systems and Hida families. The targets (Castella–Hsieh 2018, Longo–Vigni 2019, Castella 2020, Kobayashi–Ota 2020) are recent results at the research frontier resting on all of these.

GeometricSatakeAndFusion.rationale: The only nearby ingredients are Tau Ceti's Tannakian reconstruction for affine group schemes over a field, root data with their duals, Witt vectors, and Mathlib's Grassmannian functor of a module. Missing are loop groups and Beilinson–Drinfeld affine Grassmannians over Div¹ of the Fargues–Fontaine curve, the Witt vector affine Grassmannian with Bhatt–Scholze projectivity and Keel's criterion, Schubert and semi-infinite geometry, relative perverse sheaves and ULA objects on diamonds, and convolution and fusion. So are the decomposition-theorem input and the integral dual-group identification. The Fargues–Scholze Satake equivalence is at the research frontier and rests on the unbuilt diamond six-operation and Bun_G theories.

GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic.rationale: Lattices, covolumes and Minkowski's first theorem are in Mathlib, and TauCeti already has integral lattices, Witt decomposition/cancellation and local quadratic-form predicates, so GN.0–GN.1 are close. Hasse–Minkowski, genera and Siegel mass formulas need a layer of graduate local-global theory, while the Oppenheim/unipotent-flow branch and Schlichting's higher hermitian K-theory each need research-level developments.

GlobalGaloisDeformations.rationale: Only the cohomological substrate exists: continuous group cohomology with cup products and Shapiro, absolute Galois groups and Chebotarev prime sets. Deformation functors, Schlessinger representability, Tate local duality, Poitou–Tate and the global Euler characteristic formula, adjoint Selmer groups and Taylor–Wiles prime selection (KW II, ACC+ §6.2) are all unbuilt, so several research-level layers sit before the targets.

GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands.rationale: The endpoints are V. Lafforgue's global Langlands parametrization and L. Lafforgue's GL_n correspondence. Both rest on algebraic stacks (Bun_G, Hecke stacks), ℓ-adic étale cohomology with Weil II purity, perverse sheaves and intersection complexes, geometric Satake, Drinfeld's lemma and a trace formula. The library has only étale morphisms and sites, sheaf-cohomology long exact sequences, function-field Riemann–Roch and Hopf-algebraic linear groups, so many unbuilt theories stand between it and these landmark theorems.

GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights.rationale: Only point heights exist: Weil heights with Northcott in Mathlib, and TauCeti's elliptic canonical height and regulator. The YZZ Gross–Zagier formula needs Shimura curves and their Jacobians, Arakelov intersection theory with admissible Green functions, heights on abelian varieties, automorphic GL₂/quaternionic representations with Waldspurger and theta kernels, incoherent Eisenstein series and CM intersection calculations. Many research-level theories must be built first.

HabiroCohomologyFoundations.rationale: The targets are Wagner's 2024–2026 q-Hodge/Habiro descent theorems and the boundary with Scholze's analytic Habiro stack, which is current research. They presuppose animated rings, filtered stable ∞-categories, derived de Rham and prismatic cohomology, q-de Rham–Witt complexes and THH over ku. Mathlib has only p-typical Witt vectors, Kähler differentials, triangulated derived categories and basic quasicategories.

HabiroCyclotomicCompletions.rationale: Mathlib already has every ingredient: cyclotomic polynomials, Hasse derivatives, primitive roots, adic completions, limits of commutative rings and topologically nilpotent elements. Only the multi-ideal cyclotomic completion and Habiro's elementary expansion, Taylor-injectivity and evaluation theorems from one 20-page paper are missing, which is less than a layer of graduate theory.

HabiroNahmSeries.rationale: Modular-function inputs such as cusps, finite-index subgroups, q-parameters and the Gaussian integral are available. The endpoints are 2021–2025 research theorems (CGZ modularity ⇒ Bloch torsion, Garoufalidis–Zagier asymptotics, GSWZ integrality) that also need the Rogers dilogarithm, Bloch groups and K₃ of number fields with finite-coefficient injectivity, Euler–Maclaurin all-orders asymptotics and number-field Habiro modules. None of these exists yet.

HabiroNumberFields.rationale: The Frobenius-glued ring of HB.6 is only a few layers from Mathlib's completions and roots of unity. The K₃-indexed modules and finite regulators need Quillen K₃ of number fields, Suslin's Bloch-group comparison, étale Chern classes and norm-residue inputs (Soulé, Merkurjev–Suslin), the cyclic quantum dilogarithm and p-adic regulators. All of these feed 2024–2025 research theorems (GSWZ, Hutchinson), and only Kummer theory, Hilbert 90 and classical unit regulators exist.

HabiroRings.rationale: The targets are Wagner's 2024–2025 relative Habiro rings and q-Witt quotient theorems, which are current research. They need arithmetic Λ-rings with Adams operations, derived completion with Appendix-B detection, E∞ cyclotomic descent, degree-zero q-Witt rings, spectral and solid variants, and the late comparison with Habiro cohomology. Mathlib supplies only p-typical Witt vectors, étale and perfect rings, adic completion and equalizers of rings.

HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas.rationale: The stages formalize Fargues–Scholze chapters VI, VII and IX (Hecke operators on Bun_G, local shtuka spaces and their cohomology), which is current research frontier. They rest on perfectoid spaces, diamonds and v-stacks, the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve, Bun_G and its Newton strata, B_dR-affine Grassmannians with geometric Satake and fusion, and solid/lisse ℓ-adic sheaves. The library has only Spa of Huber pairs, isocrystals over Witt vectors and condensed modules.

HeegnerPointEulerSystems.rationale: TauCeti has Mordell–Weil, 2-Selmer groups, canonical heights and abstract class-formation layers. Kolyvagin's theorem and its anticyclotomic refinements (Howard, W. Zhang, BCGS 2026) also need ring class fields, CM theory and CM points on X₀(N) and Shimura curves, modular parametrizations (hence modularity), Néron models, Tate–Poitou duality, Kolyvagin systems, Cornut–Vatsal nonvanishing and an anticyclotomic main conjecture, so many research-level layers are unbuilt.

HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions.rationale: Weil heights with Northcott, elliptic Mordell–Weil and Selmer groups, scheme-theoretic abelian varieties and Brauer groups of fields exist, so the height machine and weak Mordell–Weil are about one graduate layer away. Brauer–Manin evaluation needs Brauer groups of schemes, adelic points and global reciprocity. Faltings, Mordell–Lang and the Ullmo–Zhang Bogomolov theorem need research-level Arakelov, Faltings-height and equidistribution theory.

HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheo.rationale: Only one-dimensional local fields, Laurent-series valuations, ramification groups for places and abstract class-formation layers exist. Neither ordinary local reciprocity nor Milnor K-theory is formalized. Kato–Parshin higher local reciprocity and existence also need Galois-cohomological duality with wild coefficients and higher topologies, and Kato–Saito global theory needs Parshin chains, higher adeles and étale fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes, so several research-level layers are unbuilt.

HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves.rationale: Totally real fields, quaternion algebras, the SL₂(ℤ) action on the upper half-plane and abelian varieties over fields are available. The targets need Shimura data and canonical models, fine moduli of abelian schemes with real multiplication and polarization modules, Deligne–Pappas integral models at ramified primes, compactifications, étale cohomology with local systems, Jacquet–Langlands and Čerednik–Drinfeld p-adic uniformization. These are many established but research-level theories, none yet built.

HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups.rationale: Only Cartier duality for finite locally free group schemes, elliptic formal groups and Spa of Huber pairs exist. The Hilbert route (T0–T5) needs p-divisible groups of abelian schemes, relative p-adic Hodge theory on the pro-étale site, perfectoid Shimura towers, Fargues/AIP canonical subgroups with explicit radii and Hilbert integral models. T6 adds the 2021–2023 logarithmic Riemann–Hilbert comparison of Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu and Boxer–Pilloni, so many deep theories are missing and part of the target is recent research.

IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration.rationale: The endpoint is Caraiani–Scholze's 2024 torsion-concentration theorem for non-compact unitary Shimura varieties as used in ACC+, which is current research frontier. It rests on PEL integral models and compactifications, Newton strata, central leaves and Igusa varieties, perfectoid Shimura towers with the Hodge–Tate period map, nearby-cycle perversity, the Igusa trace formula and higher-rank Galois systems. Only isocrystals, finite group-scheme Cartier duality and abstract Hecke rings exist.

IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants.rationale: Mathlib already has Roby's polynomial laws, divided powers and Cayley–Hamilton, and TauCeti has GL₂ Hecke rings and Chebotarev prime sets. Still missing are Chenevier determinants with Cayley–Hamilton quotients and reconstruction, generalized matrix algebras, nilpotence of Hecke actions on derived endomorphisms, and Chebotarev-density interpolation. The 2023 DKSW residually indistinguishable Ribet method adds Fitting ideals, Buchsbaum–Rim complexes and rational cohomology of algebraic groups. That is about two layers of research-level algebra.

IntegralIwasawaTheory.rationale: Mathlib has Weierstrass preparation, Bernoulli numbers, cyclotomic discriminants and the Dedekind-zeta residue, and TauCeti has abstract class-formation layers, but neither has global class field theory for ℤ_p-extensions, Λ-module invariants or p-adic L-functions. Beyond classical growth and Vandiver arguments, the endpoints are Mazur–Wiles/Wiles (Hecke algebras, Eisenstein ideals, modular Galois representations), the 2023 Dasgupta–Kakde/DKSW Brumer–Stark proofs and Kurihara's 2025 all-prime determinant main conjecture. These are research-frontier results on many unbuilt theories.

InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.rationale: Abstract Galois categories with fibre functors, finite étale algebras, polynomial Galois groups and permutation triples are available. Still to be built: the étale fundamental group of schemes with its homotopy exact sequence and tame specialization (SGA 1), Hilbert irreducibility, the Riemann existence theorem with rigidity and descent, Hurwitz spaces, and Shafarevich's solvable realization theorem via embedding problems and Galois cohomology. That is several layers of established research-level theory.

K2SymbolsBrauer.rationale: Transvections, group homology H₂, tensor algebras, K₀ of abelian categories and Kummer maps exist, but Steinberg groups, K₂, Milnor K-theory and tame symbols do not. Steinberg groups, Matsumoto's theorem, tame symbols, Bass–Tate and Weil reciprocity are about one to two layers of graduate theory. The arithmetic stages (K₂(O_F) via localization, the plus-construction comparison and Tate's K₂/Galois-cohomology theorem with Hilbert-symbol reciprocity) also need Quillen K-theory and class field theory.

K3BlochGroups.rationale: Group homology in all degrees, elementary matrices and Schur multipliers exist, but there is no Quillen K-theory, plus construction or Steinberg group. The targets need K₃ as H₃ of the Steinberg group via Hurewicz, Milnor versus indecomposable K₃, Suslin's Bloch–Wigner sequence via configuration complexes and homology stability, Quillen's finite-field computation, Lee–Szczarba's K₃(ℤ)=ℤ/48 and Borel-type arithmetic for K₃(ℚ(i)). These are several layers of established research-level theory.

KTheoryFiniteLocalFields.rationale: Finite fields, orders of finite general linear groups, local fields and Witt vectors exist, but only K₀ is formalized. Quillen's finite-field computation needs higher K-theory spectra, topological K-theory with Bott periodicity, Brauer lifting and Adams operations. Local higher K-theory needs Gabber–Suslin rigidity, Moore's local K₂ and the Hesselholt–Madsen/Geisser–Hesselholt THH/TC and de Rham–Witt calculations, so many research-level homotopical theories are missing.

KTheoryLowDegrees.rationale: Most objects exist: projective modules with locally constant rank, Picard groups of commutative rings, ideal class groups, determinants, exterior powers and transvections in Mathlib, plus K₀ of exact/abelian categories and the Cartan map in TauCeti. Ring K₀ with its λ-structure, the Steinitz rank/determinant splitting, stable GL with Whitehead's lemma, K₁ and SK₁ are one layer of standard graduate theory. Bass–Milnor–Serre's SK₁(O_{F,S})=0, K₀ of regular curves and the π₀K/π₁BGL⁺ comparisons add some research-level work.

KatoEulerSystems.rationale: Only analytic modular-form inputs exist: Dedekind eta products, Eisenstein series, GL₂ Hecke operators and continuous group cohomology. Kato's zeta elements and explicit reciprocity law also need Siegel units on arithmetic modular curves over ℤ[1/N], K₂ symbols with étale Chern classes, étale cohomology with modular local systems and Hochschild–Serre, p-adic Hodge theory (Bloch–Kato/Perrin-Riou regulators), modular-symbol p-adic L-functions, Rohrlich-type nonvanishing and Euler-system descent. Many deep theories are unbuilt.

LanglandsParameterStacks.rationale: Root data, GL-type Weyl modules, Hopf-algebraic affine group schemes and abelian continuous cohomology exist. The targets are the 2020–2025 moduli of Langlands parameters (Fargues–Scholze VIII/X, Dat–Helm–Kurinczuk–Moss, Zhu). They need Weil groups with discretizations, nonabelian condensed cocycles, lci representability of the cocycle scheme, derived quotient stacks and Perf, excursion algebras, and integral reductive invariant theory with good filtrations and Donkin subgroups. That is recent research on many unbuilt foundations.

LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles.rationale: Schemes with smooth and proper morphisms, Proj, étale and pro-étale sites, henselian local rings and symplectic groups exist, but there is no ℓ-adic étale cohomology. The classical targets (SGA 7 nearby and vanishing cycles, Picard–Lefschetz, Lefschetz pencils, Deligne's open symplectic monodromy, BBD perverse t-exactness, Weil II invariant cycles) sit on étale cohomology with proper/smooth base change and finiteness theorems, quasi-unipotence and ℓ-adic Lie-group arguments. That is several unbuilt layers.

LocalGaloisDeformationRings.rationale: Mathlib has Fontaine's θ with B_dR⁺, Grassmannian functors and continuous cohomology, and TauCeti has finite locally free group schemes with Cartier duality. Kisin's potentially semistable deformation rings, finite-flat and Barsotti–Tate component analysis, dyadic cases and the n-dimensional ordinary/Fontaine–Laffaille conditions of ACC+ also need local deformation functors with Schlessinger representability, crystalline/semistable period rings and admissibility, Breuil–Kisin modules, rigid generic fibres and lattice moduli. That is several research-level layers.

LocallyAnalyticDistributions.rationale: Mathlib already has abstract p-adic measures with the bounded Amice transform and the Mahler basis, and TauCeti has compact and Fredholm operators. Still missing: locally analytic function spaces with their compact-type inductive-limit topology, the unbounded Amice transform, Amice–Vélu/Vishik admissible distributions, Schneider–Teitelbaum character spaces over affinoids, and Serre–Coleman Fredholm determinants with slope decompositions. That is about two layers of graduate-to-research p-adic functional analysis.

LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory.rationale: Mathlib's model theory already supplies languages, structures, ultraproducts with Łoś's theorem, the ring language with ACF completeness, and Diophantine sets including exponentiation, so LD.0 and much of MRDP are close. Valued-field languages with AKE/Denef–Pas elimination, Denef's p-adic cell decomposition and Igusa-zeta rationality, Cluckers–Loeser motivic integration, o-minimal cell decomposition with Pila–Wilkie, and source-scoped unlikely-intersection applications are several research-level layers.

MetaplecticAutomorphicForms.rationale: Symplectic groups, Schwartz functions with the Fourier transform and Poisson summation over ℝ, the Jacobi theta transformation law and the adele ring exist. Everything metaplectic is missing: Heisenberg groups and Stone–von Neumann, the metaplectic cover with Weil indices, Schwartz–Bruhat models over local fields and adeles, dual-pair splittings and local theta modules, genuine automorphic forms with theta kernels, half-integral weight forms, and Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein Eisenstein series on the GSp(4) cover. That is several layers of established research-level theory.

ModularCurvesPartII.rationale: TauCeti's analytic layer (Γ₀/Γ₁ Hecke operators, newforms, Petersson products) and Mathlib's Weierstrass ℘-function exist, but the baseline has no modular curve as a scheme, since PR81's Katz–Mazur affine curves are not merged. The targets need complex uniformisation with analytification and GAGA, Deligne–Rapoport/Conrad generalized elliptic curves on algebraic stacks with coarse spaces, Tate curves and regular models of bad fibres, Jacobians as abelian varieties, étale H¹ with Ihara's lemma and the modular quotients A_f, which is several layers of established research-level arithmetic geometry.

ModularIwasawaMainConjectures.rationale: The endpoints are Fouquet–Wan's universal-family and cohomological main conjectures (2021–2024 preprint), the 2025 Burungale–Castella–Skinner ordinary theorem and the Lei–Loeffler–Zerbes signed comparisons, which is current research. They rest on Λ-module structure theory with characteristic ideals, Greenberg and signed Selmer complexes with determinants, Kato's zeta elements and Euler-system bounds, Skinner–Urban and Fouquet–Wan unitary Eisenstein congruences, Hida families and Wach-module Coleman maps, while the library has only power-series Weierstrass division, continuous cohomology and descent Selmer groups of elliptic curves.

ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions.rationale: Cusp-form L-functions with the Mellin formula (Mathlib), Γ₀/Γ₁ Hecke operators with nebentypus and newforms (TauCeti) and the bounded Amice transform are available. Missing are modular and Manin symbols at arbitrary level with Eichler–Shimura period maps, integral period lattices and twisted critical values (one graduate layer), plus locally analytic distributions with Stevens' small-slope control theorem and, for the critical-slope targets, the Pollack–Stevens theta sequence and Bellaïche's eigencurve local algebra, which rest on the unbuilt eigencurve.

ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions.rationale: The endpoints are Newton–Thorne symmetric-power functoriality (2021, Hilbert case 2026), the Arthur/Mok/Kaletha–Mínguez–Shin–White endoscopic classifications with their conditional inputs, and potential automorphy, all at the research frontier. They rest on automorphic representations of GL_n and classical groups, the stabilized twisted trace formula and fundamental lemma, Galois representations of automorphic forms with modularity lifting, and Rankin–Selberg and symmetric-power L-functions, while the library has only classical newforms, Dirichlet L-function nonvanishing, Frobenius prime sets and adeles.

MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles.rationale: Mathlib has algebraic cycles with pushforward and Karoubi envelopes, and TauCeti has Weil divisors as cycles and Tannakian reconstruction for affine group schemes, but there are no Chow groups, rational equivalence or refined intersection products. Chow and numerical motives with Jannsen's semisimplicity need intersection theory and a Weil cohomology with cycle classes (itself étale or de Rham cohomology with comparisons), and Voevodsky's geometric motives, Nori diagram categories and motivic Galois groups are further research-level layers; the cycle conjectures are only to be stated.

MotivicEtaleKTheory.rationale: Hilbert 90 and low-degree group cohomology, continuous Galois cohomology with Kummer classes, Brauer groups of fields, étale sites and K₀ exist, but there is no higher algebraic K-theory, Milnor K-theory, étale cohomology of schemes or motivic cohomology. The targets (Tate's K₂ theorem, Bloch's higher Chow groups with the moving lemma, the Rost–Voevodsky norm-residue theorem with sheaves with transfers, motivic Steenrod operations and norm varieties, the Friedlander–Suslin/Levine motivic spectral sequence and Quillen–Lichtenbaum via étale descent) are established theorems, but they rest on many research-level theories not yet built.

NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties.rationale: Mathlib has smooth morphisms and equation-level reduction types of Weierstrass curves, and Tau Ceti has abelian varieties over a field, DVR models of curves and the combinatorial Picard group of a fibre's intersection matrix. There are no abelian schemes, Néron models or smoothening, no Tate modules of abelian varieties, and no semiabelian schemes, Raynaud extensions or generalised Jacobians. The targets (BLR, SGA 7 IX, Faltings–Chai degeneration) need several research-level layers on top of the missing abelian-scheme, formal/rigid-geometry and Tate-module theory. The good/semistable Galois comparisons of R11.5 also need p-adic Hodge theory.

NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa.rationale: Mathlib supplies generic Ore localization, Weierstrass preparation for power series and continuous group cohomology, and Tau Ceti has K₀ of abelian categories. There are no completed group rings of p-adic Lie groups, no K₁ or relative K₀ of rings with localization sequences, no reduced norms or SK₁, no commutative main conjecture and no p-adic L-functions of totally real fields. The targets are Kakde's and Ritter–Weiss's equivariant main conjectures, extended by uniqueness results from 2025–2026: frontier theorems resting on many unbuilt theories.

OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLif.rationale: Tau Ceti has classical Hecke, U_p and diamond operators on Γ₀(N)/Γ₁(N) forms and eigenforms, but there are no ordinary projectors, Iwasawa/weight-space algebras, Hilbert modular forms, Galois representations attached to modular forms, deformation rings, pseudorepresentations or patching. Hida theory and the Skinner–Wiles residually reducible R=T theorems sit on top of all of these, together with p-adic Hodge input (Berger–Li–Zhu).

OverconvergentAutomorphicForms.rationale: Tau Ceti has Huber rings and the adic spectrum Spa with rational subsets and a structure presheaf, and Mathlib has ring-level perfectoid constructions such as θ and B_dR^+. There are no adic or perfectoid spaces, no Hodge–Tate period map, no Hilbert modular varieties or forms, no weight spaces or locally analytic representations and no toroidal compactifications. The endpoint (Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams 2023, compared with Andreatta–Iovita–Pilloni) is recent research resting on all of these.

PELModuli.rationale: Tau Ceti supplies the linear-algebra and group inputs: polarized Hodge structures, the split symplectic group scheme with its reductivity, and isogenies of abelian varieties over a field. There are no algebraic spaces or stacks and no Artin representability, no abelian schemes with polarizations, Rosati involutions or level structures, no Weil pairings, no deformation theory of abelian schemes and no Shimura varieties. Lan's and Kottwitz's constructions rest on many of these unbuilt theories. The generic-fibre comparison and canonical-model stages (M3–M4) also need Baily–Borel/Borel algebraicity and the theory of complex multiplication.

PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomo.rationale: Mathlib has Kähler differentials and one-dimensional isocrystals over W(k)[1/p], and Tau Ceti has Huber rings and restricted (Tate) power series. There are no Robba rings, dagger algebras or differential modules with Frobenius, no slope filtrations, formal schemes, tubes or overconvergent isocrystals, and no rigid or crystalline cohomology. Kedlaya's local monodromy, finiteness and p-adic Weil II theorems, and the comparison with ℓ-adic purity, rest on many layers of research-level theory.

PadicFamilies.rationale: Mathlib's Fitting decomposition gives the finite-level input to the ordinary projector, Mahler's basis describes continuous functions on ℤ_p, and Tau Ceti has classical U_p operators and q-expansions. There are no p-adic or Λ-adic modular forms, no ordinary Hecke algebras, no compact operators or Fredholm determinants on p-adic Banach modules, no rigid-analytic modular curves, modular symbols, eigenvarieties, p-adic L-functions or big Galois representations. The Coleman–Mazur/Buzzard eigenvariety machine and the Pollack–Stevens/Bellaïche family L-functions need many research-level layers built first.

PadicHodgeRegulators.rationale: Mathlib has B_dR^+ as a ring, Teichmüller lifts in Witt vectors, and p-adic measures on ℤ_p with the Amice transform. Tau Ceti adds Teichmüller roots of unity in local fields. There is no algebraic K₃ or derived p-completion, no Bloch group, p-adic logarithm or polylogarithm, no syntomic cohomology or étale regulators, and no Bloch–Kato exponentials, (φ,Γ)- or Wach modules, or Perrin-Riou logarithm. The targets combine the 2024–25 Garoufalidis–Scholze–Wheeler–Zagier unramified K₃ theorem with Perrin-Riou/LLZ regulator theory resting on many unbuilt theories.

PadicHodgeTheory.rationale: Mathlib has ℂ_p, the tilt, Fontaine's θ, and B_dR^+ and B_dR as bare rings. There is no filtration, topology or Galois action on B_dR, and no B_cris, B_st, period functors, filtered (φ,N)-modules or weak admissibility. Fontaine–Laffaille modules, Robba rings, relative period sheaves and crystalline/semistable comparison are also missing. The targets combine Colmez–Fontaine, the p-adic monodromy theorem, Kisin's potentially semistable deformation rings and Scholze/Česnavičius–Koshikawa comparisons, needing many research-level layers.

PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp.rationale: Tau Ceti has smooth discrete modules for continuous cohomology and Peter–Weyl theory for compact groups. There are no smooth admissible or unitary Banach representations of p-adic groups, no locally analytic vectors, and no Robba rings, (φ,Γ)-modules or Galois deformation rings. Colmez's functor, Paškūnas's projective envelopes and the Breuil–Mézard results of Paškūnas, Hu–Tan and Tung are frontier theorems resting on all of these unbuilt theories.

PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras.rationale: Mathlib already has abstract measures as continuous duals of C(X,R), the Mahler basis, the Amice transform D(ℤ_p,ℤ_p) ≃ ℤ_p⟦X⟧, Weierstrass preparation and profinite groups. Still missing is about one graduate layer: completed group rings with convolution, pseudo-measures, the structure theorem, characteristic ideals and μ/λ invariants for Λ-modules, and determinant lines of perfect complexes. The rigid character-space stage L0a additionally needs rigid geometry that is not yet built.

PerfectoidQuotients.rationale: Mathlib has perfections and the tilt, Witt vectors with Fontaine's θ, and the naive two-term cotangent complex. There are no integral perfectoid rings, almost mathematics, δ-rings or prisms, no simplicial commutative rings, derived cotangent complex or derived p-completion, and no prismatic cohomology or Hodge–Tate comparison. The endpoint (Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 7.4, and Theorem 5.8 of Scholze's Étale cohomology of diamonds) is recent research resting on all of these, plus André's flatness lemma.

PerfectoidShimuraVarieties.rationale: Tau Ceti has adic spectra of Huber pairs and reductive group schemes, and Mathlib has the Grassmannian functor and tilts. There are no Shimura varieties or canonical models, no minimal or toroidal compactifications, no perfectoid spaces, diamonds or pro-étale sites, no canonical subgroups and no Hodge–Tate period maps. The targets (Scholze 2015, Hansen–Johansson 2023, Boxer–Pilloni §4.4) are frontier results resting on all of these.

PerfectoidSpaces.rationale: Tau Ceti has built Huber pairs and Tate rings, the adic spectrum with rational subsets, and a structure presheaf on Spa with a rational-cover sheaf criterion. Mathlib has the tilt, the multiplicative untilt map and θ. There is no sheafiness theorem or adic space, and no almost ring theory, perfectoid Tate rings, tilting equivalence, almost purity or perfectoid étale site. The later stages (limits, pro-étale presentations, finite quotients, torsor descent) need Scholze's diamond-era results and the prismatic quotient theorem: several research-level layers.

PeriodsAndSpecialValues.rationale: Mathlib has Euler's values ζ(2k), ζ at negative integers and Dirichlet L-functions, and Tau Ceti has L-series of modular forms and pure Hodge structures. There are no motives or realizations, no comparison periods, Nori period torsor or relative de Rham cohomology with Gauss–Manin connection, no higher K-theory regulators or fundamental lines, and no multiple zeta values. The roadmap assembles Deligne, Beilinson/Bloch–Kato and equivariant Tamagawa formulations with Brown's mixed Tate theorem and mirror-symmetry Frobenius computations. It sits on fourteen prerequisite roadmaps, many at the research frontier.

PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology.rationale: Mathlib provides continuous group cohomology, the cyclotomic character, Witt vectors and the Amice transform on ℤ_p⟦X⟧. There is no field of norms, no cyclotomic period ring A_K or B_K, no overconvergent or Robba ring, no étale (φ,Γ)-module or Fontaine equivalence, and no Herr complex, ψ operator, Iwasawa cohomology or Wach module. Fontaine, Cherbonnier–Colmez, Herr, Berger and Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao are established research theorems needing several such layers.

Polylogarithms.rationale: Mathlib has the complex logarithm and argument, Bernoulli functions and the Dirichlet regulator of a number field (the weight-one case), and Tau Ceti has the Euler product of the Dedekind zeta function. There are no polylogarithms or Bloch–Wigner function, no Bloch groups or higher algebraic K-theory, no Borel regulator and no Goncharov complexes. The single-valued polylogarithms are graduate analysis, but the proved endpoints are Bloch's weight-two and Goncharov's weight-three regulator comparisons. These rest on Borel's theorem, Suslin's K₃ theory and motivic cohomology, none of which is built.

PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure.rationale: Tau Ceti has Frobenius prime sets and an auxiliary-prime selection lemma for Chebotarev arguments, plus classical GL₂ Hecke operators, and Mathlib has ultrafilters. There are no arithmetic locally symmetric spaces or Borel–Serre complexes, and no Galois representations attached to torsion classes. Integral Weyl modules and Fontaine–Laffaille degree shifting, Galois deformation rings and derived or ultraproduct patching are also absent. The source (Allen et al., Annals 2023) is a frontier theorem combining Scholze and Caraiani–Scholze torsion results with Calegari–Geraghty patching.

PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems.rationale: Tau Ceti has Chebotarev Frobenius prime sets, abstract class formations and abelian varieties over a field. There is no Moret-Bailly/Skolem theorem, no Hilbert–Blumenthal moduli or torsion twists, and no Galois representations of Hilbert modular forms. Galois deformation rings, modularity lifting and compatible systems of ℓ-adic representations are also missing. Taylor's potential modularity and the Khare–Wintenberger lift and compatible-system theorems are established research results resting on many of these unbuilt layers.

PrismaticCohomology.rationale: Mathlib has divided-power structures, the Witt-vector Frobenius, derived categories of abelian categories and the naive cotangent complex. There are no δ-rings, prisms or prismatic sites, no animated rings or derived p-completion, and no formal schemes or crystalline cohomology. Nygaard filtrations, the Cartier–Witt stack, prismatic F-crystals and log structures are also missing. The targets include absolute and logarithmic prismatic cohomology and the crystalline F-crystal equivalence (2022–2025), frontier results resting on many unbuilt theories.

ProbabilisticAndMetricNumberTheory.rationale: Mathlib supplies the measure-theoretic and probabilistic base: Borel–Cantelli, Lévy's continuity theorem, ergodicity of circle maps, continued fractions, Dirichlet approximation, Chebyshev functions and ω(n). Tau Ceti adds mean ergodic theorems. Missing is a graduate layer (Weyl's criterion, discrepancy, Mertens' estimates, Turán–Kubilius, Erdős–Kac, Khintchine, the Gauss measure). The modern endpoints (Koukoulopoulos–Maynard, Matomäki–Radziwiłł) are research-level but mostly self-contained analytic and combinatorial arguments.

QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms.rationale: Mathlib already has the Euler product for the partition generating function, the Dedekind eta function, Jacobi theta functions with their functional equations, and heterogeneous vertex operators. The formal q-series stage is nearly in reach, but there are no Jacobi forms or half-integral multiplier systems, no Kloosterman sums or Rademacher series, and no harmonic Maass forms, ξ-operator or Zwegers completions. The moonshine stage needs vertex operator algebras, the Monster and Borcherds's proof, so research layers of very different depths remain.

RankZeroOneBSD.rationale: Tau Ceti has proved Mordell–Weil over number fields, with 2-Selmer groups, weak Mordell–Weil and the Néron–Tate regulator, and Mathlib has reduction types of Weierstrass curves. There is no L-function of E/ℚ or its modular continuation, and no Tate–Shafarevich group, Tamagawa factor or real period. Heegner points, Gross–Zagier, Kolyvagin systems and Iwasawa main conjectures are also missing. The prime-part formulas (Jetchev–Skinner–Wan, Castella, Castella–Grossi–Skinner, Burungale–Skinner–Tian–Wan) are frontier results sitting on twenty prerequisite roadmaps.

ReductiveGroupsPartII.rationale: Tau Ceti has reductive affine group schemes over fields, abstract Tits systems with Bruhat cells, and split classical groups, and Mathlib has root pairings and their duals. There is no topology on E-points of schemes and no Weil restriction. Relative and valued root data, Bruhat–Tits buildings, parahoric group schemes, Cartan/Iwasawa decompositions over local fields and L-groups are also missing. Bruhat–Tits I/II is a research-level theory needing several layers (Borel–Tits relative theory, valued root data, integral models) on top of the field-level foundations.

RefinedTraceMethods.rationale: Mathlib has quasicategories, the Dold–Kan correspondence and Kähler differentials, and Tau Ceti has A∞-algebras. There is no Hochschild, cyclic or periodic cyclic homology, and no stable ∞-categories, spectra, THH with circle action, Tate constructions or TC. The cyclotomic trace, topological K-theory ku/KU and localizing motives are also missing. The targets run from Nikolaus–Scholze and the Beilinson fiber square to 2024–2026 refined TC and Habiro comparisons (Wagner, Meyer–Wagner, Efimov): frontier work resting on many unbuilt homotopy-theoretic foundations.

RelativeFarguesFontaine.rationale: Mathlib has p-typical Witt vectors with Teichmüller lifts, tilts and Proj of graded rings, and Tau Ceti has adic spectra of Huber pairs. There are no ramified Witt vectors W_{O_E}, no adic or perfectoid spaces, diamonds or v-sheaves, and no relative period spaces 𝒴_S and Y_S or Frobenius quotient X_S. Divisor moduli with B_dR sheaves and Beauville–Laszlo gluing are also missing. The target is the relative curve of Fargues–Scholze (2021/2026), a frontier construction resting on all of these unbuilt theories.

SchemeAndStackFoundations.rationale: The SF.0 layer is largely in Mathlib: schemes, flat/étale/smooth/proper/separated morphisms, quasi-coherent modules, big Zariski/étale/fpqc topologies and sheaf cohomology on sites. Tau Ceti adds Riemann–Roch consequences for function fields and Abel–Jacobi classes of Weil divisors. Several substantial layers are missing: algebraic spaces and stacks with effective descent, étale base-change theorems, Picard schemes, formal schemes and deformation theory, Chow groups and intersection theory, and de Jong's alterations.

SchemeKTheoryOperations.rationale: Tau Ceti has K₀ of abelian and exact categories and Weil divisors as algebraic cycles, and Mathlib has derived categories and sheaves of modules on schemes. There is no higher algebraic K-theory (Quillen or Waldhausen), and no perfect complexes on schemes or enhancements. K/G-theory with supports and localisation, Nisnevich descent, Gersten complexes, λ- and Adams operations, Chern classes, Chow groups and Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch are also missing.
