The Thomason–Trobaugh and SGA 6 theory is established but needs several research-level layers (spectra, enhanced categories, intersection theory) first.

SelmerIwasawaCohomology.rationale: Mathlib has continuous group cohomology, and Tau Ceti adds its functoriality, continuous inflation–restriction, Tate cohomology, the Kummer sequence and 2-Selmer groups of elliptic curves. There is no local Tate duality or Poitou–Tate, no derived-limit theory for compact coefficients and no Selmer structures or complexes. Iwasawa cohomology, control theorems and Bloch–Kato local conditions are also missing. The core (Greenberg, Nekovář) needs several layers of graduate and research-level Galois cohomology, and L4 additionally needs p-adic period rings.

SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation.rationale: Tau Ceti has classical newforms, degeneracy (level-raising) maps and Atkin–Lehner operators on Γ₀(N). There are no Galois representations attached to modular forms, no Katz modular forms mod p, theta operators or Hasse invariants, and no Jacobians of modular or Shimura curves with their character groups. Ihara's lemma, finite flat group schemes and Serre weights are also missing. Ribet's and Edixhoven's theorems and the Buzzard/Wiese dyadic cases are established research results resting on many of these unbuilt layers.

ShimuraCompactifications.rationale: Tau Ceti has lattice-rational cones, finite fans with fan morphisms and the complex points of affine toric charts, and Mathlib has pointed cones. There are no arithmetic-admissible infinite fans or relative torus embeddings, and no Shimura varieties, minimal compactifications or mixed Shimura data. Complex-analytic gluing, semi-abelian degenerations, the Tate curve, algebraic spaces and PEL moduli are also missing. The AMRT, Pink, Faltings–Chai and Lan constructions are established research theorems resting on many of these unbuilt layers.

ShimuraData.rationale: Tau Ceti has pure Hodge structures with conjugation, points of period domains and reductive group schemes, and Mathlib has the upper half-plane and adele rings. The missing material is mostly graduate but spans several layers: Weil restriction and the Deligne torus, the equivalence of Deligne-torus representations with Hodge structures, and Cartan involutions with Hermitian symmetric domains. Homogeneous variations of Hodge structure, compact duals with reflex fields, and the category of Shimura data with neat levels are also needed, with little research-level input (Deligne 1979 §2.1, Milne §§1–5).

ShimuraVarieties.rationale: Mathlib has the upper half-plane with the SL₂(ℤ) fundamental domain, congruence subgroups and adele rings, and Tau Ceti has abstract class formations. There are no adelic double quotients Sh_K(G,X), no reduction theory or strong approximation for reductive groups, and no complex analytic spaces or GAGA. The Baily–Borel compactification, Borel's extension theorem, the main theorem of complex multiplication and canonical models are also missing. The Deligne–Milne canonical-model theorem for all Shimura data rests on many of these research-level layers.

SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns.rationale: Mathlib has a Selberg sieve carrier, Dirichlet's theorem on primes in progressions, non-vanishing of Dirichlet L-functions on Re s ≥ 1 and Chebyshev functions. Brun's sieve and the fundamental lemma, the large sieve, Vaughan's identity, Siegel–Walfisz and Bombieri–Vinogradov are all missing. Maynard's bounded-gaps theorem needs these graduate analytic layers, and the Chen and affine-sieve stages add parity-breaking bilinear estimates and expander theory (Bourgain–Gamburd–Sarnak).

SmallRamificationAndAbelianVarietyBaseCa.rationale: Mathlib has Minkowski's discriminant bound, Hermite finiteness and different ideals. Tau Ceti has elementary Chebyshev bounds, finite locally free group schemes with Cartier duality and abelian varieties over a field. The discriminant stages are close, but Fontaine's and Schoof's theorems need Fontaine's ramification bound for finite flat group schemes over ℤ_p, Tate modules, Néron models and semistable reduction. The terminal cases also use potential modularity and ordinary lifting, so several research-level layers are missing.

SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups.rationale: Mathlib has abstract double-coset Hecke rings and algebraic induction with Frobenius reciprocity, and Tau Ceti has smooth discrete modules over profinite groups. There is no category of smooth representations of locally profinite groups, no C_c^∞ Hecke algebra with idempotents, and no compact or parabolic induction, Jacquet functors or second adjointness. Admissibility, the Bernstein decomposition and center, the Satake transform and Bernstein–Zelevinsky/co-Whittaker theory are also missing. The early stages are graduate theory, but Bernstein's theory, Helm's integral families and the Dat–Helm–Kurinczuk–Moss finiteness (built on parameter stacks and excursion operators) add several research-level layers.

SpecialValuesBirchTate.rationale: Only the analytic scaffolding of the base case exists: Mathlib has the Dedekind zeta L-series (no continuation to s = -1) and zeta(-1) = -1/12 via Bernoulli numbers, but neither library has K_2 of rings of integers, Tate's K_2/Galois-cohomology comparison, Iwasawa modules or main conjectures. The headline all-prime theorem for every totally real field combines Wiles's main conjecture with Kurihara's 2025 theorem and a Kurihara-to-Kolster comparison that the roadmap itself says is still to be proved, on top of the ArithmeticKTheory and IntegralIwasawaTheory programmes (both 9).

StableHomotopyKTheory.rationale: The simplicial and unstable starting points exist: Mathlib has nerves, geometric realisation, Kan complexes, group homology and spectral objects, and TauCeti has K(G,1) spaces with basepoint-change and loop-space API for homotopy groups. Everything the roadmap owns is missing, though: homotopy-fibre long exact sequences, Quillen's Theorems A and B, the plus construction, group completion, spectra with the stable homotopy category and S-construction deloopings, and Bockstein/lim^1 sequences. That is several layers of standard graduate homotopy theory, but no research-level input.

TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure.rationale: Beyond Huber rings with Spa and abstract Hecke rings, neither library has any supplier object this roadmap compares: no perfectoid spaces or almost mathematics, Shimura varieties, Hodge–Tate period map, automorphic bundles, completed cohomology or locally symmetric spaces. Every target is a comparison on objects owned by supplier programmes rated 7–10 (PerfectoidShimuraVarieties and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII at 10), for Scholze's 2015 torsion theorem, and the symplectic branch stays conditional on Arthur's classification.

TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic.rationale: Mathlib has multiplicative ring seminorms, Gauss norms that are absolute values on K[X], and ℂ_p. Tau Ceti has the adic closed polydisc with its classical points and Riemann–Roch for function fields. There are no Berkovich spectra or analytic spaces, no metric graphs or graph Riemann–Roch, no semistable or formal models and skeleta, no tropicalization, and no model metrics or Chambert-Loir measures. Several layers of research-level nonarchimedean geometry must be built before the faithful-tropicalization and measure targets.

VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories.rationale: The library has condensed modules with a provisional solidity predicate, 1-categorical derived categories and Tau Ceti's smooth discrete representations. It has no diamonds or v-stacks, no enhanced sheaf categories with six operations, no ULA or lisse sheaves, no solid derived categories and no Bun_G. The targets are the sheaf-theoretic chapters of Fargues–Scholze (IV, V, VII), research-frontier results resting on the unbuilt ECD six-operation, enhanced-category and Bun_G theories.

VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals.rationale: Mathlib has Witt vectors and the Dieudonné–Manin classification of one-dimensional isocrystals, plus locally free sheaves of modules. Tau Ceti has Brauer groups with division-algebra representatives and affinoid adic spectra of Huber pairs. There is no Fargues–Fontaine curve (absolute or relative), no degree/slope or Harder–Narasimhan theory for its bundles, no perfectoid spaces or diamonds and no Banach–Colmez spaces. Apart from the classical VB0, the targets are research-level Fargues–Fontaine, Kedlaya–Liu and Fargues–Scholze results resting on those unbuilt theories.

WeightsInEtaleCohomology.rationale: Mathlib has only the definitions at the bottom: the small étale and pro-étale sites, sheaf cohomology as Ext, and H^n(X, Z_ℓ) with no theorems beyond the empty-scheme case. TauCeti has reached deg(1 − π_q) = #E(F_q) but not the Hasse bound. There are no finiteness or base-change theorems, Frobenius actions, weights, nearby cycles or Lefschetz pencils. The targets are Deligne's Weil I/II purity and weight theorems and their eigenform applications, imported from DeligneWeightsAndPurity, EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves and LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles (rated 9, 9 and 8), so this interface is as far away as its suppliers.

WeilConjectures.rationale: The inputs present are Mathlib's bare definition of ℓ-adic cohomology, the elliptic local factor defined from point counts, TauCeti's Riemann–Roch for function fields with class-number finiteness, and the first step of the Hasse bound. Neither library has zeta functions of varieties over finite fields, the trace formula, étale Poincaré duality or Deligne's purity, so rationality with its cohomological factorisation, the functional equation, RH and ℓ-independence all wait on the DeligneWeightsAndPurity, EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves and LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles suppliers (rated 9, 9 and 8). Only the power-sum and point-count arithmetic is near.

tauceti:Completed/ContourIntegration.rationale: The roadmap is complete and its headline theorems are in Tau Ceti: the Hungerbühler–Wasem generalized residue theorem (single curve and null-homologous cycles, plus the simple-pole form), HW Propositions 2.2 and 2.3, the classical residue theorem, the argument principle and the homology Cauchy theorem all exist in TauCeti/Analysis/Contour, and no file under that directory contains sorry. What is absent is only generalisation beyond the pinned scope (the paper's accumulation-free singular sets and essential singularities), so nothing remains to build.

tauceti:Completed/EffectiveBounds.rationale: Every headline target of the roadmap is present and sorry-free in Tau Ceti: the discriminant bound from an integral basis, the X²·2ⁿ ideal count, h_F ≤ |d_F|·4ⁿ, the unit-square index bound, the measure-free doubling engine and the summit, an explicit count of number fields of bounded discriminant; they sit on Mathlib's Minkowski theory and Hermite finiteness. The score is 1 rather than 0 only because the Layer-3 explicit regulator lower bounds are proved just for unit rank zero, and the aspirational Brauer–Siegel theorem is absent.

tauceti:Completed/IntegralLattices.rationale: Every layer of the roadmap is already formalized in Tau Ceti under TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice: the headline gluing theorem (Nikulin's Proposition 1.4.1, A_{L_H} isometric to H^perp/H), the even-overlattice/isotropic-subgroup order isomorphism, the index/discriminant formula, all ADE discriminant-form rows and the explicit isometry E8 = D8^+. Only Mathlib's carrier and duality primitives are used underneath; nothing remains to build.

tauceti:Completed/OrthogonalL2Bases.rationale: The roadmap is completed. Every headline target is a Tau Ceti declaration with no sorry: the Hermite L²(ℝ) basis and its Gaussian-measure counterpart, the moment-determinacy completeness lemma, the orthogonality-relation→HilbertBasis bridges and weighted-L² isometry, the L² product and pi bases, the multidimensional Hermite bases, and the Chebyshev basis with its cosine transfer. The Fourier-eigenfunction and oscillator extras are also proved.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces.rationale: Tau Ceti already covers Layers 0–2: Huber and Tate rings, weighted restricted series, topological localisation, Henkel's open mapping theorem, spectral Spv(A,I), Cont A and Spa(A,A⁺), and rational subsets. It also has much of Layers 3–4: Lemma 8.1, a presentation-indexed structure presheaf and the flatness chain up to Corollary 8.32. Still missing is one layer of standard theory (Tate acyclicity, Buzzard–Verberkmoes, noetherianity of Tate algebras, the category of (pre-)adic spaces with gluing). On top of that sits the Fargues–Fontaine application, which rests on Kedlaya's research-level noetherianity of interval rings.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCodingTh.rationale: All prerequisites are present (Mathlib's Hamming distance, dot-product orthogonals and finite-field additive characters; Tau Ceti's completed integral-lattice gluing theory and coordinate-power finite quadratic modules), but Tau Ceti's coding layer so far only fixes the carriers and generator/parity-check matrices. Minimum distance, puncturing/shortening, weight enumerators and MacWilliams, Type II codes, the Golay/hexacode/tetracode computations and Construction A — one layer of standard textbook theory plus explicit finite verification — are still to be built.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves.rationale: The headline theorem is already proved: Tau Ceti has a sorry-free function-field Riemann–Roch with the whole Stichtenoth Ch. 1 chain (product formula, genus, Weil differentials and canonical class, strong approximation, Weierstrass gaps, finite Cl⁰ over finite constants), much of the extension theory (fundamental identity, conorm, different divisor with tame exponent and tower law) and the elliptic point–place dictionary. What is left is roughly one layer of standard graduate theory: the cotrace and Hurwitz genus formula, constant-field extensions, the hyperelliptic and plane-curve genus formulas, Weierstrass points and the 84(g−1) bound, and the curves ↔ function-fields dictionary with its cohomological comparison.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology.rationale: The singular-chain layer is in place (Mathlib's singular homology with homotopy invariance and H_0, CW complexes, cubical homotopy groups, spectral-sequence framework; Tau Ceti's relative singular homology with pair and triple long exact sequences, local coefficient systems, and the generation half of groupoid van Kampen), but every headline theorem is missing: excision/Mayer-Vietoris, cellular homology, cohomology products and Poincare duality, Kunneth and Serre spectral sequences, Hurewicz and Whitehead. These are several stacked layers of standard graduate textbook theory, not research-level theory.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AnalyticToricGeom.rationale: Tau Ceti already has the combinatorial supplier: integral lattices, toric and regular cones with primitive rays, finite fans with morphisms, products and subdivisions. It also has the first analytic inputs: characters, the generator-independent topology on affine complex points, and holomorphic mixed monomial maps. Mathlib supplies scheme and topological gluing, manifolds and proper maps. What is missing is one layer of standard graduate toric geometry (Fulton ch. 1–2, Cox–Little–Schenck ch. 1 and 3): dual semigroups and affine toric schemes, glued fan schemes and complex manifolds, the orbit–cone correspondence and toric boundary, the properness criterion and the algebraic–analytic comparison.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichl.rationale: Tau Ceti already proves, sorry-free, Layers 0–5 (ideal arithmetic functions and weights, norm regrouping, convolution and Möbius, ideal Euler products and logarithmic derivatives, two-sided ideal counts with abscissa 1, higher-prime-power and residue-degree estimates), most of Layer 6 (Abel summation, truncated Perron, the ϑ→π transfer), natural density, Landau/3-4-1 positivity and the smoothed Wiener–Ikehara limit. What remains is standard and less than one layer: the Tauberian passage to the sharp wienerIkehara, the Dirichlet-density bound predicates, calculus and all-prime normalization, the cancellation continuation, and the packaged PNT transfer.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/BelyiMaps.rationale: Tau Ceti has the finite base (permutation triples with genus, and bipartite ribbon graphs) and strong generic suppliers: the finite-cover/π₁-set equivalence, and one-variable function fields with ramification and Riemann–Roch. The headline results are a different matter. Analytic Riemann existence for three-point covers, Belyi's theorem with descent to ℚ̄, fields of moduli, and the faithful Galois action and branch-cycle theorem on the profinite π₁ of ℙ¹∖{0,1,∞} all need theories absent from both libraries: compact Riemann surfaces and branched covers, Seifert–van Kampen, the analytic–algebraic comparison, Weil descent for pairs, and the arithmetic fundamental group with its outer action. That is several layers of advanced graduate theory, though none of the targets sits at the research frontier.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CFSGStatement.rationale: The named statement is largely assembled in Tau Ceti: I0 indices, all 26 sporadic presentations, and fixed-point candidate groups on explicit carriers for every Lie-type family except ³D₄, ²G₂, ²F₄ and the Tits group. Still missing are those four branches (the tripled D₄ carrier and the short-root carriers with their special isogenies), the A0 assembly of ClassificationStatement, and the L4/L5 identifications. These need Mathlib's suzukiGroup, which is not in the baseline, and the full isomorphism theorem for pinned groups; so far only the Kostant ℤ-form group schemes and a uniqueness lemma exist.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev.rationale: The algebraic scaffolding is already sorry-free in Tau Ceti: Artin symbols with tower and restriction laws, conjugacy-class powers, Frobenius prime sets and ramified primes, the cyclotomic Frobenius formula, Galois-character weights with orthogonality, the auxiliary prime, compositum splitting and tagged fibres, fixed-field Frobenius fibre counts, and the Frobenius von Mangoldt coefficient with its o(x) discard estimate. What is missing is the analytic heart and every density or counting conclusion: continuation and nonvanishing at s = 1 of cyclotomic character series (which needs the absent power-saving ray-class ideal counts), plus the Dirichlet-density calculus and sharp Wiener–Ikehara step it consumes, together about one layer of standard graduate theory.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory.rationale: Tau Ceti supplies only the scaffolding: formations, normal layers, restriction/inflation towers and abelian layers (Layer 1 and part of Layer 4), low-degree Tate identifications (Ĥ⁰ = norm quotient, Ĥ⁻² ≃ G^ab), cyclic periodicity, a Herbrand quotient, low-degree continuous cup products and Brauer groups of central simple algebras. Everything from Tate's theorem onward is absent (class formations and fundamental classes, the local invariant and local reciprocity, local existence and the Weil group, the Brauer sequence, global reciprocity and existence, the Hasse norm theorem, class fields, Kronecker–Weber and Hilbert reciprocity), which is several layers of standard graduate, but not research-level, theory.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.rationale: Tau Ceti already has the grid objects and the first milestones of Lanes G and L: grid diagrams and states, integral bigradings, the fully blocked, simply blocked and unblocked complexes with d^2 = 0, the graded Euler characteristic as a grid determinant, grid links as diagrams modulo moves, and F_2[U] lattice homology with a nonzero U-tower. The headline results still need several layers of self-contained but research-level combinatorics: commutation and stabilization invariance, the bigraded F[U]-module structure theorem and tau, the Milnor conjecture and slice-genus bound, sign assignments, and the whole OSS stable HF-hat theory, for which no Heegaard diagram layer exists.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ConformalMapping.rationale: Tau Ceti already has the summit and layers L0–L5: Rouché, Hurwitz, Morera, Montel and Vitali; Schwarz–Pick and the Poincaré disc; the Riemann mapping theorem; Schwarz reflection and the monodromy theorem; and Carathéodory's theorem for Jordan domains. What remains is L6, the global Schwarz–Christoffel theorem: its integrand, primitive and boundary edges exist, but not the conformal map onto a prescribed polygon or the prevertex parameter problem. That is one standard textbook theorem resting on layers already built.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/DGAInfinity.rationale: Tau Ceti covers the algebra-level start of Layers 0-3: the Koszul-signed symmetric monoidal structure and linear Hom enrichment on cochain complexes, the Stasheff/bar-coderivation equivalence, DG algebras and modules with functorial cohomology, nonunital A-infinity algebras with units, augmentations, cohomology and strict morphisms, and normalization of contractions. Mathlib supplies derived and triangulated categories. Everything after that is still missing: general A-infinity morphisms, A-infinity and DG categories and modules, homotopy transfer and Kadeishvili's theorem, bar-cobar, twisted complexes, derived Morita theory, DG quotients, Hochschild and deformation theory, smooth/proper and Calabi-Yau structures, and Koszul duality. These are several layers of research-level homological algebra.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/DenseGraphLimits.rationale: Tau Ceti already proves the basic layers: graphons, homomorphism densities, the cut norm, a cut distance that satisfies the triangle inequality on any probability space, the graphon-space metric quotient, both counting lemmas, Frieze–Kannan weak regularity, total boundedness, agreement of the coupling and map forms of the cut distance, Goodman/Mantel/Sidorenko-C4, and the setup for sampling and exchangeable graph laws. What is missing is one layer of standard results from Lovász's monograph: completeness and compactness of graphon space, inverse counting (separation), the equivalence of the two convergence notions, Lovász–Szegedy representability, and the Diaconis–Janson mixture representation. The tools these need (martingales, Prokhorov, McDiarmid) are already available.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves.rationale: Tau Ceti already proves the headline Mordell–Weil theorem over number fields, together with canonical heights, the regulator, explicit 2-descent and Nagell–Lutz, and has a function-field isogeny theory with Frobenius, [n] of degree n² and deg(1 − π_q) = #E(𝔽_q). Several layers of standard graduate theory (AEC/ATAEC) are still missing and none is research-level: the dual isogeny and the Hasse bound itself, E[N] with the Weil pairing and Tate modules, Tate's algorithm, conductors and the Tate curve, H¹-classified twists, global minimal models, and cohomological Selmer groups and Sha.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability.rationale: Tau Ceti proves the v1 summit (de Finetti–Ryll-Nardzewski, in the conditionally-i.i.d. form) by all three routes. It also proves reverse-martingale convergence, the uniqueness, empirical-measure, zero-one/ergodic/extreme-point interfaces, Hewitt–Savage, finite de Finetti, the countable-index version and the Diaconis–Freedman Markov-exchangeable representation. The only headline item still missing is the hard converse of the Aldous–Hoover representation for exchangeable arrays; its easy direction and the row-coding and dissociation infrastructure are already present.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/FuchsianOrbifolds.rationale: Only the base of Layer 0 exists: the PSL(2,ℝ) action on ℍ with continuity, a proper orbit map and cyclic stabilizers in Tau Ceti, and proper discontinuity of discrete SL(2,ℝ) subgroups and bare cusp predicates in Mathlib. Neither library has quotient or compactified Riemann surfaces, orbifold charts, hyperbolic polygons with the Poincaré polygon theorem, degree theory, Riemann–Hurwitz or Euler characteristics of compact surfaces, or X(1) ≅ ℙ¹. That is two or three layers of standard graduate theory (Fuchsian geometry and compact Riemann surfaces) still to build, though the complex-analytic inputs from ConformalMapping and ContourIntegration are available.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GeometricTopology.rationale: The goal is to state, not prove, the Kirby-list results, and Tau Ceti has started the lower layers: the boundary as a manifold with local smooth collars, locally flat embeddings and local bicollars, the PL groupoid, Diff(M) as a group, knot presentations with Seifert-matrix and Burau Alexander invariants and the signature, slope arithmetic, combinatorial manifolds, and the Zeeman statement. The constructions the statements need are still missing: global collars, tubular neighbourhoods, boundary gluing and connected sum, knot complements and Dehn filling, the C-infinity topology on Diff(M), concordance, Riemannian volume, curvature and hyperbolic volume, model geometries and JSJ, Heegaard genus, and foliations with their Euler class. That is several layers of graduate differential, PL and 3-manifold topology, plus some research-level definitions.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberField.rationale: Layers 0–2 are essentially in Tau Ceti, sorry-free: normalized absolute values with the product formula over all places, mixed Artin–Whaples weak approximation with sign control, moduli and ray class groups with idealClass, the intrinsic triviality criterion, classMap, finiteness, the class number formula, exact sequences and the narrow comparison; discreteness of K in 𝔸_K is also proved and Mathlib supplies the adele and idele carriers. Missing is a broad band of standard graduate theory: power-saving ray-class ideal counts, strong approximation and compactness of 𝔸_K/K and of the norm-one idele classes, the idele norm and congruence subgroups with the ray-class dictionary, continuous adelic base change, Hecke characters and infinity types, cyclotomic ray-class identifications, and orders with Pic/NarrowPic.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalQuadraticFo.rationale: Tau Ceti already has this roadmap's Layer 0 (localization at every place, the local isotropy/representation/equivalence predicates, complex-place automaticity), plus field-generic Witt cancellation and decomposition, the real signature classification and weak approximation into completions. Neither library has the local Hilbert symbol, Hasse invariant or p-adic classification of forms, nor the global class-field inputs the proofs consume (Hilbert reciprocity, the Hasse norm theorem, the idele-class norm index), so Hasse–Minkowski, existence and classification over number fields sit behind about three layers of standard graduate theory, one of them the heavy global class field theory layer.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GrothendieckEuler.rationale: Tau Ceti already has the core of every layer: Quillen exact structures; split, exact, abelian, triangulated and graded K₀ with universal properties; the horseshoe lemma and the projective resolution theorem; the Cartan isomorphism under finite projective resolutions; Ext-Euler descent with the dual-numbers rejection; the q-sesquilinear graded Euler form; and numerical quotients. What remains is standard graduate material: the general resolving-subcategory resolution theorem, the bounded homotopy/derived K₀ comparisons, Cartan-matrix bases and unimodularity, the graded Cartan map and linear resolutions, q = ±1 specialization, and the quiver comparisons and examples.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer.rationale: Tau Ceti has made a real start on the lowest analytic layers: Fredholm operators and index stability, finite-dimensional Morse-Sard, Sard-Smale, the Morse lemma and index, gradient flows, and definitions of almost complex structures and pseudoholomorphic maps. Every headline object is still missing, and so is every layer under it: stable manifolds and Morse-Smale transversality, trajectory compactness and gluing, the Cauchy-Riemann elliptic package and spectral-flow index theorem, Gromov compactness, J-curve transversality and gluing, Lagrangian Floer homology, and Sym^g geometry with Heegaard diagrams and spin^c structures.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HodgeStructures.rationale: All four milestones are proved, sorry-free, in TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/ (841 declarations): the L0 Hodge decomposition, L1 semisimplicity of polarizable rational Hodge structures, L2 strictness of mixed Hodge morphisms through an explicitly defined Deligne splitting, and L3 period-domain points with Hodge numbers summing to the rank. The worked instances (Tate structures and twists, effective weight one, the Weil operator, the lattice isometry group) are there as well. Mathlib itself still has no Hodge-theoretic declarations.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HopfRinow.rationale: Layer 0 and much of Layer 1 are in place: the piecewise-C^1 and C^1 Riemannian distances agree, the distance is finite on connected manifolds, lower semicontinuity of length holds, and Tau Ceti adds C^infinity regularity of Mathlib's Levi-Civita connection, the geodesic predicate, a smooth geodesic spray, maximal intervals with homogeneity, constant speed, the manifold inverse function theorem and metric length-space API. What is missing is about one layer of standard graduate Riemannian geometry: smooth dependence of the geodesic flow, the exponential map and its derivative, normal neighbourhoods, the Gauss lemma, minimizing geodesics and the Hopf-Rinow equivalence itself.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge.rationale: Tau Ceti already has abelian varieties over a field (dimension, base change, tangent space), abstract divisor-class Pic⁰ with degree splitting and a divisor-level Abel–Jacobi class, function-field genus and Riemann–Roch spaces, and basic cohomology of sheaves of modules on schemes. What is missing is the scheme-theoretic core: finiteness of coherent cohomology, Serre duality, cohomology and base change, fppf descent, symmetric powers of curves, the relative Picard functor and its representability, and the dual abelian variety and theorem of the cube. These are several layers of heavy theory below the Jacobian itself.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamifi.rationale: Mathlib has the IsNonarchimedeanLocalField class, spectral norms and Krasner's lemma, and Tau Ceti covers much of Layers 0–1: the normalized valuation and absolute value, the unit filtration and its graded pieces, the Teichmüller section, and openness of power subgroups in the tame regime. The canonical valuative structure on finite extensions and the intrinsic e and f are still missing, as are unramified extensions with Frobenius and K^ur ≅ Ẑ, lower and upper ramification groups, Herbrand functions, Hasse–Arf, the local different, the deep-unit logarithm and the Iwasawa presentation of the tame quotient. That is roughly one book of standard graduate theory (Serre's Local Fields).

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves.rationale: The library has scheme morphism properties, locally constant flat rank, relative normalization and the Hopf-algebra/affine-group-scheme correspondence (Mathlib). Tau Ceti adds Cartier duality for finite locally free commutative affine group schemes and the equation-level isogeny theory over a field, including deg [N] = N². Nothing yet exists on elliptic curves as group schemes over an arbitrary base: no projective Weierstrass scheme model, relative Picard/Poincaré duality, scheme-theoretic Weil pairing, Drinfeld level structures, Katz–Mazur moduli formalism, fppf quotients, deformation theory, p-divisible groups, Serre–Tate theory, regularity theorems or coarse moduli. The roadmap also presupposes the missing coherent-cohomology-and-base-change stack of the Jacobian roadmap, so the Katz–Mazur targets sit on many research-level layers still to be built.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms.rationale: Mathlib supplies modular and cusp forms, q-expansions and the level-one dimension formula. Tau Ceti already covers much of Layers 0–7: diamond operators and the nebentypus decomposition, the GL₂ Hecke ring and Hecke operators with U_p = T_p, Petersson adjoints and the old/new complement, newforms with the Main Lemma and strong multiplicity one, normalized Atkin–Lehner and Fricke operators, valence formulas and the finite-index Sturm bound, and entire continuation of cusp-form L-series. Still missing are Eisenstein series with character, the newform Euler product and functional equation, the modular-symbol integral Hecke algebra (coefficient field is a number field), Galois stability and LMFDB invariants, analytic Riemann–Roch on X(Γ) with the general dimension formulas, and the Eichler–Selberg trace formula. That is more than one layer of graduate theory, though none of it is research-level.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Multiquadratic.rationale: All four layers of the roadmap are already in Tau Ceti: the 2ⁿ degree theorem, the Galois group (ℤ/2)ⁿ and its subfield lattice, the Frobenius and splitting law, the ambiguous class number, the genus field (ordinary, real and narrow) with its maximality, and the isomorphism Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)². Both 2-rank formulas are proved, together with the worked examples ℚ(√−5) and ℚ(√−21). Only the optional long-horizon items (Hilbert class field, ring class fields) are left, and they belong to class field theory.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithm.rationale: Mathlib's number-field library is strong, and Tau Ceti already has most of Layers 1–4. That includes the Artin symbol with its restriction and tower formulas, the ideal-theoretic Artin map, the double-coset bijection for non-Galois splitting, the relative Kummer–Dedekind theorem, the power-basis index formula, the relative discriminant ideal with tower law and ramified support, Stickelberger's congruence, monogenicity, and the completion algebra map with local-field instances. Still to build are Dedekind's cycle-type theorem and criterion, the semilocal completion dictionary (norm/trace, decomposition group as local Galois group, completed integer rings, localization of the different), the global higher-ramification exponent formulas (which need the local ramification roadmap), unit certificates and label semantics. This is less than a full layer of standard graduate theory.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/OneParameterSemig.rationale: Every milestone of the three parts is already in Tau Ceti, built on Mathlib's LinearPMap, Bochner integral and Fourier theory. That covers the Hille–Yosida and Lumer–Phillips generation theorems (both as characterizations), Stone's theorem, classical solutions of the Cauchy problem, Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder with uniqueness, Lévy–Khintchine uniqueness for Bernstein functions, Bochner's theorem on finite-dimensional inner-product spaces, and the Berg–Christensen–Ressel theorem with uniqueness. Only the stated stretch goal, Bochner on locally compact abelian groups, is left.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport.rationale: Tau Ceti has built most of the common spine (Layers 0–3) on Mathlib's probability measures, kernels, Prokhorov and KL divergence. That covers couplings, gluing and multi-marginal plans, extended transport cost with compactness, existence and stability, finite and compact/lower-semicontinuous Kantorovich duality, c-transforms and cyclical monotonicity, the Wasserstein distance and space with completeness, quantile couplings and weak convergence, and basic Monge costs. Almost all named summits are still absent: Brenier/McCann (no extended convex conjugate API), Aleksandrov/Caffarelli/MTW/partial Monge–Ampère regularity, Lisini superposition and Benamou–Brenier, AGS gradient flows and JKO, barycenters, entropic transport and Sinkhorn, CD/RCD synthetic curvature, and Gromov–Wasserstein. Several of these are research-level and also wait on unbuilt PDE and Riemannian roadmaps.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE.rationale: Mathlib provides distributions, Bessel-potential Sobolev spaces, Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev and Lax–Milgram. Tau Ceti has built much of Lanes A and D: weak derivatives and W^{k,p} and W^{1,p}_0 spaces, Poincaré on bounded slabs and balls, Rellich–Kondrachov compactness, complete Hölder spaces, uniform ellipticity with Gårding's inequality, weak Dirichlet existence and uniqueness, the Fredholm alternative and Dirichlet eigenvalues. It also has the Hardy–Littlewood maximal function and the Newtonian kernel. Missing are the trace operator and Morrey embedding, Marcinkiewicz/Riesz–Thorin interpolation, Calderón–Zygmund and BMO, maximum principles and the Hopf lemma for general operators, Perron's method, H²/Schauder/De Giorgi–Nash–Moser regularity, and the parabolic Galerkin and heat-semigroup lane. That is a couple of layers of standard graduate PDE theory.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PolynomialGaloisG.rationale: Mathlib has Polynomial.Gal with its faithful root action and Chambert-Loir's block and primitivity library. Tau Ceti already has much of Layers 0–4: the orbit/irreducible-factor dictionary and transitivity-iff-irreducible, stabilizers as relative Galois groups, the block–intermediate-field order isomorphism and 2-transitivity criterion, the discriminant test for containment in Aₙ, the universal resolvent with its symmetric-polynomial specialization, general wreath products, and the n ≤ 5 reference subgroups with the nTj label predicate. What remains is classical: the classification of transitive subgroups of degree ≤ 5, the quartic and quintic resolvent decision tables and quintic certificates, Jordan's p-cycle theorem, the imported Dedekind factorization theorem (whose supplier is not yet built), and the three-prime realization of Sₙ.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomolo.rationale: Mathlib supplies discrete group cohomology, finite-level Hilbert 90 and the canonical continuousCohomology carrier. Tau Ceti has built much of the explicit low-degree layer: H⁰, H¹, H² with comparison to discrete groupCohomology (and to the canonical carrier in degree 0), finite-quotient colimits in degrees 0 and 1, the low-degree long exact sequence with δ-naturality, corestriction to degree 2, Shapiro in degrees 0–1, the six low-degree cups with the projection formula, and Kummer cocycles. Still missing are the degree-1/2 comparisons with the canonical carrier, the five-term sequence with transgression, profinite Hilbert 90 and the Kummer isomorphism, the all-degree theory (colimit, long exact sequence, Shapiro, corestriction), cohomological dimension, the graded cup product and the Evens norm. That is about one further layer of standard graduate Galois cohomology.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGrou.rationale: Mathlib has ProfiniteGrp with limits and completions, finite Sylow theory and Frattini subgroups. Tau Ceti has built most of Layers 0–3: supernatural order and index with Lagrange, profinite Sylow existence, containment and conjugacy, the maximal pro-p quotient with its universal property, the pro-p Frattini subgroup with Burnside, topological finite generation and the Hopfian property. Still missing are free profinite and free pro-p groups with their universal properties, presentations with extensions, embedding problems and the H¹/H² rank interpretations, Golod–Shafarevich, cohomological dimension of pro-p groups including Serre's freeness theorem, Demushkin groups with duality and orientation, the central-tower comparison method, and Labute's classification. These form several layers of advanced graduate-to-research theory that also depend on unfinished continuous-cohomology infrastructure.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/QuadraticFormInva.rationale: Mathlib supplies quadratic forms, diagonalization, quaternion algebras and the Brauer group carrier. Tau Ceti has built Layers 0–1 and part of 2–3: the RegularFormClass carrier with discriminants, chain equivalence of diagonal forms, Witt decomposition, cancellation and extension, hyperbolic planes, Cartan–Dieudonné, the quaternion norm form with split and Steinberg relations, and a nontrivial quaternion Brauer class. Missing are the Witt ring with its fundamental ideal and Pfister forms, the four-fold splitting criterion, the Hasse and Clifford invariants, the quadratic defect and local Hilbert symbol, the local classification by (dim, d, s), the crossed-product comparison Br(K)[2] ≅ H²(G_K, μ₂) with the cup–norm theorem, Stiefel–Whitney classes, and the Scharlau transfer with Kahn's relative formula. These layers sit on the unfinished local-field, continuous-cohomology and class-field-theory suppliers, and Kahn's formula is research-level.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups.rationale: Mathlib supplies Hopf algebras, group objects, abstract root data and Coxeter groups. Tau Ceti has built most of Layers 0–6 over a field: the Hopf/affine-group-scheme dictionary and functor of points, comodules with Tannakian reconstruction, Hopf ideals, fppf quotients and components, tangent spaces, Jordan decomposition, multiplicative-type groups and tori, unipotent and solvable radicals with Lie–Kolchin, and the reductive and semisimple predicates. It also has pieces of Layer 7: existence of geometric Borel subgroups, dynamic parabolics and Levi decompositions, GLₙ root data, torus-level special isogenies. Still missing are conjugacy of Borel subgroups and maximal tori, the root datum and Bruhat decomposition of a general reductive group, the isomorphism and existence (classification) theorems, and the explicitly constructed pinned Chevalley–Demazure group schemes over ℤ with root subgroups and the G₂/F₄ special isogenies. These are several deep layers of SGA 3–level theory.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationThe.rationale: This index page has no targets of its own, so its distance is the median over its twelve sub-roadmaps as classified in this batch: SemisimpleAlgebras 0; CharacterTheory, CompactGroups, RootSystems 1; InductionRestriction, LieHighestWeight, QuiverRepresentations, SchurWeyl, SpinRepresentations 2; AdoIwasawa, ClassicalGroups 3; LieGroups 5. Tau Ceti already covers most of the finite-group, compact-group (Peter–Weyl), symmetric-group, root-system and semisimple-Lie-algebra cores. The farthest lanes are the smooth Lie-group correspondence, the group-level classical-group classification and Ado–Iwasawa.

Mathlib has the Lie-algebra substrate: enveloping algebras, nilpotent and solvable ideals, Engel and Lie's theorems, semidirect sums, and the generalized Krull intersection theorem. Tau Ceti adds the PBW filtration with ordered-monomial spanning, the associated-graded comparison map, and Weyl complete reducibility for Killing algebras. Still missing is one layer of textbook theory (Jacobson, Ch. VI): PBW injectivity for non-abelian L, the nilradical, derivations lifted to U(L), Levi decomposition, and central p-polynomials, followed by the Ado–Iwasawa–Hochschild theorems themselves.

Deliverables A–C are essentially built in Tau Ceti on top of Mathlib's characters and row orthogonality. That covers class functions, completeness, #irreducibles = #classes, Σ nᵢ² = |G| and nᵢ ∣ |G|, the Galois action, the Dixon–Schneider specification with uniqueness, good-prime existence, and a certified rational/cyclotomic solver. Most of D is also done: the Frobenius–Schur trichotomy, Burnside's pᵃqᵇ theorem, Frobenius kernels, and the GL₂(𝔽_q) principal series, Steinberg and linear rows. What remains is the cuspidal series of GL₂(𝔽_q) with its irreducibility and the assembled full table.

Tau Ceti has built most of the scaffolding. That includes the standard representations of GLₙ, SLₙ, Oₙ and Spₙ, polynomial tensor, symmetric and exterior powers, and Young-symmetrizer Weyl modules. It also has the GLₙ/Sₘ double-centralizer theorem, torus weight decompositions, Schur polynomials, the Weyl and hook-content dimension numbers with Gelfand–Tsetlin pattern counts, and the 𝔤𝔩ₙ Lie-algebra highest-weight existence theorems. Still missing is the representation-theoretic layer of Fulton–Harris and Goodman–Wallach: the highest-weight classification of rational GLₙ, SOₙ and Spₙ irreducibles, characters as Schur polynomials, the dimension theorem for Vλ, and the branching isomorphisms with the Gelfand–Tsetlin basis and generators.

Tau Ceti has built the roadmap through its summit on top of Mathlib's Haar measure and Hilbert-basis API. That covers Haar averaging and unitarizability, complete reducibility, matrix coefficients with Schur orthogonality, the Peter–Weyl theorem as peterWeylBasis with Parseval, and the character Hilbert basis with isotypic projectors. The SU(2) engine case is there too: torus conjugacy, the Sym^d classification, and Weyl-character closed forms with torus-side orthonormality. What remains is the measure-theoretic Weyl integration formula on SU(2), which the source file explicitly leaves out, and the packaged G×G decomposition L²(G) ≅ ⨁ End(V_π).

Mathlib provides the Ind/Res/Coind adjunctions. Tau Ceti has built Layers 0–5 on top of them: transitivity, the projection formula, the induced-character formula and Frobenius reciprocity for characters, the Mackey decomposition as a natural isomorphism, Mackey's irreducibility criterion, and Clifford theory. It also has most of Layers 6–7: the representation ring, Artin's induction theorem and Artin's corollary, and projective representations classified by H² with twisted group algebras. What remains is a textbook chunk: Brauer's integral induction theorem over (hyper)elementary subgroups, Brauer's characterization of characters, the ℚ(ζ_e) splitting-field corollary, and Schur representation groups (covers).

Mathlib has only the LieGroup class and left-invariant derivations. Tau Ceti adds Deliverable A's first half: the Lie exponential as a local diffeomorphism at 0, classification of one-parameter subgroups, Ad/ad with Ad∘exp = exp∘ad, the Lie functor with faithfulness, the Lie subalgebra of a closed subgroup with its limit criterion, and a Banach-algebra local BCH. Still missing are several layers of standard graduate Lie theory: the embedded closed-subgroup theorem and group-level BCH, Frobenius integrability and Lie's third theorem, simply connected covers, compact maximal-torus conjugacy with general Weyl integration, complexification, Borel–Weil and Bruhat, and the Cartan/Iwasawa/KAK decompositions.

Mathlib reaches the Killing root system and sl₂ triples. Tau Ceti has built the representation theory on that base: Verma modules and L(λ), the dominant-integral classification of finite-dimensional irreducibles, Weyl complete reducibility, Weyl invariance of characters with the Weyl denominator and numerator identities, central characters, Freudenthal's formula, the full 𝔤𝔩ₙ layer, and carriers for the octonions, the Albert algebra and E₆/E₇ minuscule modules. Still missing, all standard (Humphreys §§17–24, Jacobson): PBW injectivity, the last step of the Weyl character formula with the dimension and Kostant formulas, the minuscule Pieri rule, the Harish-Chandra isomorphism, the Serre-presentation isomorphism, and identifying the exceptional models with LieAlgebra.g₂…e₈.

Mathlib gives quivers, paths and Morita equivalence. Tau Ceti has built most of Layers 0–5: path algebras with admissible ideals and basic algebras, quiver representations as modules, Krull–Schmidt, projective covers and injective envelopes, Euler/Tits forms and BGP reflection and Coxeter functors, and uniqueness of indecomposables by dimension vector. It also proves 'positive-definite Tits form ⇒ finite type with #indecomposables ≤ #positive roots' and has Kronecker/one-loop counterexamples, the AR translate and a Kronecker almost-split sequence. Still missing is textbook material: the converse (finite type ⇒ ADE) with the indecomposable ↔ positive-root bijection in general, Gabriel's presentation theorem, and general existence of AR sequences with the AR quiver.

Mathlib has RootPairing, bases, Cartan matrices, Weyl groups and CoxeterSystem. Tau Ceti has built nearly all of Layers 1–6 on top: positive roots and inversions, the Coxeter matrix of a base with the surjection from the presented Coxeter group, strong exchange and Bruhat order, dominant chambers as a fundamental domain, the longest element, the finite-type Cartan-matrix classification into valid Dynkin types with rigidity, and simply connected root data. What remains is small: Tits' injectivity (the full weylCoxeterSystem), coordinate realizations proving each Dynkin type exists, base-independence of the type, and the Aₙ ↦ Sₙ₊₁ and G₂ ↦ Dih₆ identifications.

Mathlib contributes Young diagrams, partitions and cycle types. Tau Ceti has built Layers 0–5 in full: dominance, Young subgroups and permutation modules, symmetrizers, Specht modules via the submodule theorem, the classification partitionEquivSimpleFDRepClasses, the standard polytabloid basis, and the hook-length formula. It also has the Sₙ character table with column orthogonality, Kostka numbers with Schur = Σ K·m, rim hooks, the GL/Sₙ double-centralizer theorem, and Brauer diagram composition with O/Sp-commuting cup/cap operators. Still missing are standard results: the Murnaghan–Nakayama rule, the Frobenius characteristic and Jacobi–Trudi, RSK, the explicit (ℂᵈ)^{⊗n} ≅ ⊕ S^λ ⊗ 𝕊^λ decomposition, and orthogonal/symplectic Schur–Weyl duality via the Brauer algebra.

Mathlib proves Artin–Wedderburn existence, Schur's lemma and isotypic decomposition. Tau Ceti has built every remaining layer. That covers invariance of the block count, simple-module classes of the regular module, the double-centralizer theorem, and tensor products of central simple algebras staying simple. It also covers A ⊗ Aᵒᵖ ≅ M_{dim A}(K), the square-dimension theorem, Skolem–Noether, the centralizer theorem, the Brauer group as a commutative group, and finite separable splitting fields, maximal subfields and the index. The roadmap is essentially complete.

Mathlib defines CliffordAlgebra, pinGroup and spinGroup. Tau Ceti has built Layers 0–4 and much of 5, 7 and 9 on top: the filtration with gr Cliff ≅ ⋀V, the structure theorem via polarizations, and Pin/Spin double covers with ℤ/2 kernels and the spinor-norm sequence. It also has the spin and half-spin modules with irreducibility and weight-space decomposition, type-B/D integral forms, Spin₃ ≅ SL₂, real Clifford algebras with the Bott isomorphism, the quadratic realization with Kostant's left-regular module, and the 𝔤𝔩_N CAR isotypy instance. Still missing: Spin₄ ≅ SL₂×SL₂, Spin₅ ≅ Sp₄ and Spin₆ ≅ SL₄, triality as an outer automorphism of Spin₈, and the general Kostant isotypy corollary with its multiplicities.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StablePeriodicCur.rationale: Mathlib supplies the triangulated homotopy and derived categories and localization. Tau Ceti adds part of Layer 0: Quillen exact structures with a Frobenius predicate, the morphism-ideal quotient, and DG right modules. Nothing beyond that exists. Missing are Happel's triangulated stable category, self-injective and Gorenstein-projective stable categories with Buchweitz's singularity-category equivalence, differential modules and periodic derived categories with Stai's hull, and curved DG modules with Positselski's derived categories of the second kind. Matrix factorizations with HMF and Orlov's comparison are missing too. That is several layers, the later ones research-level.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction.rationale: Mathlib has schemes, fibres, the valuative criteria and DVRs. Tau Ceti has only the first scaffolding under Curves/StableReduction: finite DVR extensions, a Model structure with isomorphisms, and the combinatorics of Stacks-style numerical types with weighted Picard groups and torsion bounds. The theorem needs the whole Jacobian lane (coherent cohomology and base change, duality, Picard schemes, ℓ-torsion of Pic⁰) plus nodal families, relative dualizing sheaves, blowups, intersection theory and Lipman resolution on arithmetic surfaces, minimal models, and Artin–Winters semistable reduction. Canonical contraction and descent, and stable maps, also remain: many layers of research-level algebraic geometry.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StandardDistribut.rationale: Layers 0–5 are essentially in Tau Ceti on top of Mathlib's Gaussian, Gamma, Beta and Poisson measures: the uniform measure, the new scalar families from Laplace to hypergeometric, pgfs, the incomplete gamma and beta functions and erf with the closed-form cdfs, the distribution relations, the multivariate Gaussian (affine maps, quadratic-form mgf, conditional law), multinomial and Dirichlet. Layer 6 already has symmetric-matrix Lebesgue measure, Cholesky with its Jacobian, the multivariate Gamma integral and the Gaussian-Gram Wishart law with its trace mgf. What remains is the real-degree density Wishart family, the spectral characteristic-function formulas, Bartlett decomposition and inverse-Wishart, which is part of one layer on existing infrastructure.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/UniversalCovers.rationale: Mathlib contributes covering maps, homotopy lifting, the lifting criterion and the fundamental groupoid. Tau Ceti has built every stage on top. That covers the based-path universal cover as a simply connected covering, the deck group with Deck(proj) ≃* π₁, and the pointed/unpointed Galois correspondence with regular covers and N(H)/H. It also covers π_n of a cover ≅ π_n of the base for n ≥ 2, π₁(S¹) ≅ ℤ, the higher homotopy of circles and tori, π₁(ℝPⁿ), and recognition of K(G,1) spaces. The roadmap is essentially complete.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ZigzagPreprojecti.rationale: Tau Ceti has built the strict-algebra half on its path-algebra API: doubled quivers, zigzag algebras with bases, dimensions, centers, nondegenerate trace pairings and self-injectivity, and graded Cartan matrices for D₄, E₈ and affine E₈. It also has additive preprojective algebras with gauge, opposite and orientation independence, plus A∞ algebras only at the level of Stasheff identities. The derived half is absent: quadratic/Koszul duality and Etingof–Eu Koszulity, 2- and 3-dimensional Ginzburg DG algebras and Calabi–Yau completions, Hochschild cohomology with minimal A∞ deformations and Liu–Wang intrinsic formality, and Khovanov–Seidel braid actions. Those are several research-level layers resting on a largely unbuilt DG/A∞ sibling roadmap.
